entities.name: Osric
entities.line: Rose from near-peasant through the Guard. Warm in public, calculating underneath, careful with every word.
entities.secret: Hides a surname linked to a prominent House within the Kingdom, suspecting corruption but unable to confirm it.

entities.name: Wendeline Brackenford
entities.line: The eldest. Keeper of customs. Gentle but stubborn.

entities.name: Fenwick Larkspur
entities.line: Ex-Guard. Blunt and practical. Respects Hesketh.

entities.name: Bertram Quillby
entities.line: Keeps the records, ledgers and tithe counts. Precise and polite.
entities.secret: **Corrupt.** His meticulous records obscure tithes being skimmed.

entities.name: Ysolde Ambergate
entities.line: Oversees harvest stores and rationing. Charming and persuasive.
entities.secret: **Corrupt.** Steers bigger harvest shares to favorites.

entities.name: Clementine Rook
entities.line: The newest Elder. Curious about magic. Deals with Murrow.

entities.name: Tobin Ashby
entities.line: Born into a smithing family. Determined, loyal, efficient. A homebody pulled toward danger. Minor strength enhancement.

entities.name: Doric
entities.line: Strict because he hates mistakes, proud of his work. Advises the Hearthcircle on metal. Forges Murrow's Featherhooks.

entities.name: Hesketh Reeve
entities.line: A human over a mostly halfling Guard. Harsh but fair, not corrupt. Dislikes weregild but upholds it.

entities.name: Murrow
entities.line: Hidden under a deep hood. Cold and businesslike, never mean. Channels other people's magic, never his own.
entities.secret: His real nature, his hidden NW home, his fear of the Kingdom, and an unrevealed soft spot.

entities.name: The Wellhouse family
entities.line: Wealthy, came centuries ago out of a soft spot for sharing. Ostracized. Keep to the tavern.

entities.name: Burn
entities.line: Short, mustached, red cap. Drops one-line roasts from his bar stool, only when it's funny, about what people do and never who they are. The Wellhouses' one friend. Swears red-capped mushrooms make you grow. A little fire magic.
entities.secret: A runaway court jester from the capital, hiding from the noble his joke offended.

entities.name: The Town Crier
entities.line: Booming, cheerful and impossible to ignore — remarkable in a halfling. Rings the bell at the market cross, calls every notice exactly as it's written, and makes a small ceremony of it. Fond of a tankard once the last call is done.

entities.name: Glumtom
entities.line: Gloomy lifelong tinkerer, drafted as a registered citizen. Heals, builds and raises undead laborers. Works *for* the Kingdom, not *with* it.
entities.secret: Distant family to Murrow. Made the Seeker's Lodestone, which could find him, but isn't looking.

entities.name: The Scribe
entities.line: Sour, unimpressed, constantly criticizing young adventurers for their lack of appetite. Secretly cares a little. Fines would-be robbers into the swear jar.

entities.name: The Wandering Clerk
entities.role: A guildscribe who broke from the hall
entities.where: The Clerk's road, out to the Woodland Road
entities.line: Keeps a ledger of their own, swears in adventurers where there's no guild, posts bounties.

entities.name: Bregga Stumpteeth
entities.line: Hawker with a gap-toothed grin, whose booming voice carries across the square.

entities.name: Widow Hesk
entities.line: "Recently widowed" for as long as anyone remembers. Sells on sympathy. No relation to Hesketh Reeve.

entities.name: Fenwick Loose-Coin
entities.line: Constantly short on coins and owing debts to many. No relation to Fenwick Larkspur.

entities.name: Marda the Reformed Cutpurse
entities.line: A former pickpocket gone straight, who won't let anyone forget it.

entities.name: Grithnall the Threadbare
entities.line: Patched from hat to boots. Claims his coat was once a lord's.

entities.name: Ossop the Unlucky
entities.line: Everything at his stall goes wrong. Buyers pity him into sales.

entities.name: Beren Halfcoat
entities.line: His coat is more pocket than garment; he’s the most honest haggler in the square.

entities.name: Ivy Scraptongue
entities.line: Trades insults with buyers and wins. Deals in scrap and workshop salvage.

entities.name: Doras Milkbeard
entities.line: White-bearded seller of "remedies" that are mostly tea.

entities.name: Ruel Tinkpocket
entities.line: A tinker with pockets full of broken parts. Fixes trinkets while he haggles.

entities.name: Podge Ashborn
entities.line: Round, cheerful and sooty. Secondhand pots, lanterns and fire-scorched goods.

entities.name: Uther Nine-Debts
entities.line: Owes nine debts to nine people. Sells fast to stay ahead of all nine.

entities.name: Wobble
entities.line: Rolling gait, a cart with one bad wheel. First to unpack, last to leave.

entities.name: Pruneface Yorik
entities.line: Wrinkled, scowling miser who drives the hardest bargains on the road.

entities.name: Tansy Ninefingers
entities.line: Lost a finger to a sack she shouldn't have opened. Turns up the most real relics.

entities.name: Old Corrin
entities.line: The oldest on the road. Knows every waystation, shortcut and story.

entities.name: Tam Pockets
entities.line: Young and quick-handed. His coat is more pocket than coat.

entities.name: Squint
entities.line: Nearsighted and won't admit it. Inspects every coin, never cheated.

entities.name: Nan Gullyfoot
entities.line: Grandmotherly, sells knitted goods, feeds anyone who looks hungry.

entities.name: Kettle
entities.line: Always has a kettle on. Gossips over every cup.

entities.name: Sella Windrags
entities.line: Cloth and scarves flap from her pack. You can see her coming a mile off.

entities.name: Arandur
entities.line: Abandoned, landless, self-taught archer. Buries everything under contempt. Talks down magic, fears trolls but can't hate them. Since pulled into another world (Midkemia, a D&D campaign world).
entities.secret: His magical abilities might be echoes of his mother, Silwen, influencing him.

entities.name: Silwen
entities.line: Taught him stealth and tracking, told him troll tales. Vanished on a "hunt."
entities.secret: Perhaps Silwen’s lingering magic influenced his abilities.

entities.name: Faelan
entities.line: Distant and rarely present. Vanished with Silwen.

entities.name: Belenos
entities.line: Nobility raised among pirates and thieves in a port city, kind by upbringing. Can take the form of a blink dog. Spots Arandur's sticky fingers.

entities.name: Ulfgar Luttenheim
entities.line: Wild magic and a natural affinity for stones.

entities.name: Órla
entities.line: The party's healer. Carries Lindwurm.

entities.name: Theron
entities.line: Has enough Arcana to read magic items.

entities.name: Kaelreth Graveborn
entities.line: Casts illusions, rides Gravehoof, keeps a notebook. His room in the wagon is the one nobody wants to enter.

entities.name: Sebastian
entities.line: A full bard who leans on persuasion spells.

entities.name: Styx
entities.line: Based on the hero of the *Styx* stealth games.

entities.name: Queen Taileflaith
entities.line: Took the throne very young. Also called Queen Tali. Her disappearance is the party's quest.

entities.name: King Pedgar
entities.line: Married the queen less than a year before she vanished. His power is still unstable.

entities.name: The Ringmaster
entities.line: Carries a whip and is "whatever she wants to be." Has a warlock pact with the fey.

entities.name: Lugh
entities.line: Belenos's fey patron, and patron and friend of the pirate kingdom.

entities.name: Morrigan
entities.line: Death's spouse. Blessed Bitterbridge against harmful fire.

entities.name: Mourgause
entities.role: Morrigan's sister, the witch of the world
entities.line: Cursed Bitterbridge's fruit bitter for five years.

entities.name: Morgana
entities.line: Under her, crows and ravens turn on the people of Bitterbridge.

entities.name: The millers (one of the wealthier families)
A regular merchant and their escort
The fishers of the lake's settlement (5 to 10 of them)
The head of House Harrowmere, who holds the Highwrit
Hearthstone

fields.limits: It draws on the latent wind in whoever holds it, so it works better for humans than halflings. Holding it for too long leaves you winded.

fields.limits: It only finds artificers. Glumtom could find Murrow with it, but he isn't looking, and Murrow doesn't know it exists.

fields.limits: Until it's finished, nothing hides him from the Seeker's Lodestone for long.

entities.name: Murrow's Shard

fields.note: Murrow's own tool, combined from six auto mode ideas
fields.where: Monstradius. Murrow keeps it on him in his coat pocket while he works, and locks it in a warded alcove in the workshop wall at night.
fields.does: Senses traces of magic. Held near a person, tool or place, it pulses warm and faintly lights up, showing thin, coloured "threads" where mana has been used recently: what kind and how strong, never who. Murrow uses it to diagnose broken enchanted items, spot anyone copying an artificer's work, and check whether someone is quietly drawing on mana. Held close to a spell as it's cast, it can briefly amplify it (a gust reaches twice as far, a healer's touch runs stronger) for a few seconds.
fields.made: A smooth, robin's-egg-sized shard of mirrorstone, etched with fine silver lines. It was part of an unfinished Rift compass belonging to Silas Brightstone, the travelling artificer Murrow apprenticed under long ago. Silas vanished while working on it near the Ashen Reach when a small rift tore open; the surge overloaded the mirrorstone and left this shard behind, and Murrow salvaged it.
fields.limits: Uses the holder's own mana, never stored mana, and it can't be charged. Range is about 10 feet, up to 30 at most, shrinking with heavy use. It only shows active or recent magic: old, faded magic and steady wards barely register, and strong elemental or divine magic drowns it out. Amplifying lasts seconds and costs about a full day's exertion. Overuse brings dizziness, chills (the shard turns painfully cold as the holder runs low), headaches, gaps in memory and brief "echoes" of other artificers' thoughts. Forcing it without an attuned mind causes painful backlash. Elves and those attuned to elemental magic find it easier to use.
fields.story: It's the heart of Murrow's study of rifts and of the Rift compass, and of his hope to store mana in objects. He believes it holds an echo of the rift that made it, and that it might one day open small, controlled rifts, though it never has. Doric is the only one allowed to examine it, and has tried and failed to copy it. Clementine Rook has been shown it a few times under strict supervision. Murrow won't say what it does.

entities.name: Artificer's mark

fields.where: On enchanted items made in the Kingdom; the register it answers to is kept in the Rolls House.
fields.does: The identifying symbol an artificer inscribes onto any magically enhanced item created within the Kingdom.
fields.rules: Every artificer the Kingdom finds goes into the register of artificers and is put to work, the way Glumtom was.
fields.limits: Unmarked items aren't illegal to own, but they make people ask who made them. Nothing from Monstradius carries one.
fields.story: Murrow's goods are a quiet risk if they ever reach the capital.

entities.name: Embercrown

fields.does: A delicate metal crown set with gems that glow like embers, worn by the Kingdom's royals at official events in the capital. Worn outside formal occasions, it stirs whispers of court gossip and intrigue around the wearer.
fields.made: Needs rare materials to craft. The ember glow is a fire user's mana stored in the gems, so like every enchanted item it runs dry and has to be charged again.
fields.limits: Royals only, and only for ceremonies. The edge of the realm never sees it, and most of the capital only ever sees the Crown's banner.
fields.story: Raises how much influence and authority people see in the wearer. Who charges it is a question for the register of artificers. Open question: where is it kept when it isn't worn? The Crown's seat beside the Rolls House is the obvious guess.

entities.name: Conduit Staff

fields.note: From a lore-keeper chat about wizard staffs
fields.where: Made at Monstradius.
fields.does: An amplification focus. Channels the ambient mana around the user into focused blasts or shields. Favoured by fire users.
fields.made: A polished obsidian core wound with silver thread and fitted with a focusing lens. Murrow oversees its making, and it takes a lot of work.
fields.limits: Drains mana quickly if overused, and grows noticeably colder as it runs low. Obsidian is brittle.
fields.story: Still open: whether Doric could reinforce the core with strands of mithril, which would be risky but powerful.

fields.does: A manipulation focus. Lets a skilled user subtly bend the magic around them, to dampen earth tremors or disrupt another spellcaster.
fields.made: Seasoned Ash wood from the Ashen Reach. Its cost depends mostly on Doric's skill in treating the wood against the weather.
fields.limits: Needs intense concentration, and risks amplifying out of control.
fields.story: Still open: whether working the ambient magic draws unwanted attention from the Monster Wood, maybe from a grove there known for attracting aberrant creatures.

fields.does: Dense, tough wood the woodworkers prize for tool handles, weapon hilts and arrow shafts.
fields.made: From the few short, twisted ash trees that grow on the Ashen Reach, the grey plain south of Stoutwell.
fields.limits: Nothing grows tall on the Reach, so it's too short for beams. The village's timber still comes from the dead-tree runs.
fields.story: Still open: whether the trees are what's left of a wood that grew there before the Reach turned grey, and who's allowed to cut them on the Guard's training grounds.

entities.name: UNIVERSE
entities.text: The Grand Orrery. It's the artificers' name for the universe, picturing its worlds as moving parts in one great mechanism. Only high-ranking and learned people know the name. Worlds connect through rifts: random tears that open and close, pulling in people, monsters or whole buildings, which is why the same monsters appear on different worlds. Some artificers can open a rift on purpose, using a doorway as the boundaries for the magic.

entities.name: WORLD
entities.text: Verrowen. This is a scholarly name found in books. Villages own few books, and only kingdoms have libraries, so common folk just say "the world."

entities.name: TONE
entities.text: Medieval fantasy with D&D-style monsters.

entities.name: MAGIC
entities.text: Common but weak. It assists work, it doesn't replace it. Types: elemental (wind, fire, earth), strength enhancement, detection. Everyday uses include mending torn or cracked things and loosening or firming soil. Healing specialists are very rare and only ever human, from humans' affinity for it; a small or medium village may have 2 or 3 at a time (Stoutwell has 2). Healers use magic to assist the body's own healing. Artificers aren't healers but can still heal, leaning on natural healing and on drawing other people's healing magic, sometimes nefariously. A fire user who can boil a pot of water counts as super skilled. Everyone has a well of mana. It refills more slowly than the body heals, and there's no visible bar. Running out (mana deprivation) causes sickness, dizziness or passing out. Fire is the opposite of cold, so a fire user low on mana grows cold, more so the emptier they are. Elves are most magical, then humans, then halflings. People can have latent magic they don't know about. Objects hold mana but can't make it. A charged item normally works only for the person whose mana is in it; a very rare ability, nearly as rare as artificing, lets an item work without its owner. Wind users are rare and far more often human. Strength enhancement is fairly common (Tobin uses it to hammer hot steel).

entities.name: ARTIFICERS
entities.text: Extremely rare. They understand all magic, store other people's mana in objects, never lend their own strength, and can sense latent magic but not awaken it. Murrow's Elemental Test: shown an array of items (a stone, a feather), an injured child he's healing is drawn to the one their secretly drawn mana reacts in, revealing their element; most people find their element on their own. A secret artificer item, the Seeker's Lodestone (a round, flat disc of mirrorstone, a rare black glass), can locate other artificers.

entities.name: ITEMS
entities.text: Hearthstones (fire-charged river stones, keep a stove warm one night per charge, still need embers; rare, pricey). Featherhooks (Doric's iron hooks with a wind pattern; halve a dragged log's weight using the holder's latent wind, better for humans; too long leaves you winded). Wardbells (on the walls; ring when something big leaves the Monster Wood; big vs small only; refreshed by a detection user every few weeks). Truthglass (quartz lens; says real or fake for coins, seals, papers, nothing more). Rift compass (secret, ~80% done, points where worlds are thin; even Murrow doesn't know how it works). The Rift compass doesn't point to a world: it shows how thick the rifts are nearby, and a needle twitching wildly means many unstable tears. It can't tell you which world a rift leads to.

entities.name: RESOURCES
entities.text: Hearthstones are charged river stones; the Truthglass is rare clear quartz; mirrorstone is rare black glass shaped by magic. Doric forges iron (Featherhook hooks to Murrow's specifications, the Guard's gear, ornate work) with a smith's hammer. Timber comes from dead-tree runs, is cut at the lumber mill and stored in the lumber yard. A few short, twisted ash trees grow on the Ashen Reach; their dense, tough wood is too short for beams but prized by the woodworkers for tool handles, weapon hilts and arrow shafts. Leather comes from the herders' cattle, worked at the tannery, and clothes everyone. The grain mill grinds flour. The fishing settlement's catch feeds Stoutwell. The halfling Guard fights behind big shields; human archers carry bows. Coin is gold, silver and copper; Murrow takes coin or barter on the same terms for everyone, and his rare items cost more than people expect.

entities.name: STOUTWELL
entities.text: A 600-year-old walled village of about 220 people: about 72% human, 28% halfling, plus the Wellhouse family, its only elves, who keep to their tavern and are ostracized. It's known for its stout ale and ornate smithing, and is named for its well, once the source of that ale. Its founding stories were never passed down. The ale never lost its potency, but once the well died and water had to be hauled from the river, the supply became very restricted; Murrow's irrigation might mean more ale for the first time in centuries (who controls it is undecided). The Wellhouse elves moved here centuries ago for their soft spot for sharing and caring, and do nothing for the village beyond the tavern. Its central well dried up 550 years ago because of the blight; the artificer Murrow recently built irrigation from the river. Gates face north, east, south and west. The west gate opens onto the croplands, the Woodland Road and the Monster Wood. Districts: NW is middle- to upper-class housing; NE is Murrow's shop Monstradius and his research building; SW is the shopping district with the Wellhouse tavern; the slums lie along the south and SE, with their own poorer housing and Doric's smithy. Near the center are the dried well and the Gathering Hall, where the Elderhold meets. Grain and lumber mills sit on the river outside the east wall; the lumber yard is inside by the east gate. South of the village lies the Ashen Reach, a plain of grey soil where nothing grows tall; it's Stoutwell's training grounds, right beside the slums along the south wall. The river flows south past the mills and opens into a lake southeast of the village. An impassable wall of mountains runs along the east and turns west along the south, past the Ashen Reach; the lake sits in its corner and no one goes over. On the lake's far shore from Stoutwell, at the foot of the mountains, is a small fishing settlement (name undecided) of usually 5 to 10 people. They fish and are a source of food for Stoutwell but aren't part of the village. SECRET: they guard and hide a passage through the mountains to an unknown place on the other side; outsiders don't know of it, and what lies beyond is undecided. The slums are there for two reasons: the ash dust and the noise of the drills make the south wall the least wanted land in the village, so it's where poorer families could afford to live; and the slums supply most of the Guard's recruits, so trainees live a short walk from the grounds.

entities.name: RACES
entities.text: Halflings are stout, thick-skinned and naturally heat-resistant (well suited to smithing), quick, quiet and lucky, and homebodies who love good food and a warm hearth. They reach adulthood around 20, live to about 150 and have children less often, so the oldest villagers are almost always halflings and the shortest in any crowd. Humans rarely pass 100; they're leaner, more attuned to elemental magic, and do about 70% of the wood chopping.

entities.name: LIFE
entities.text: Children are schooled together, then the Elders place them into groups (Village Workers, Herders, Farmers, Gatherers, the Guard, the Hearthcircle). People may switch jobs within reason. Heavy jobs like smithing lean male, but nothing is restricted by gender. Village Workers stay inside the walls: smiths, the tannery, woodworkers (weapon hilts, ornate structures). Herders mainly raise cattle; the Elders keep a couple of cows just to look at. Farmers work the croplands, which take up the most space. Gatherers also forage at the forest edge, and the human gatherers gather the stout ale's ingredients. The village is communal and peaceful, with little internal trouble. Homes burn firewood. Gatherers find dead trees with detection magic and drag them out with wind magic, under Guard escort.

entities.name: DEFENSE AND LAW
entities.text: The Guard is stout halfling shield-bearers plus human archers on the walls. Villagers rotate a couple of days a month between four posts (inside the village, the croplands, the walls, and escorting gathering groups), around a full-time Guard of men and women picked for strength. The guard tithe pays for it: each household gives a share of its harvest, crafts or labor, and wealthier families like the millers give more. The halfling Guard is small and overworked, which shows as a little skimming and shift dodging; the extreme punishments keep defiance minimal. Hesketh dislikes weregild but accepts it because it's the law. Punishments range from stocks and flogging to exile and execution. Weregild (payment in place of punishment) is accepted.

entities.name: LEADERSHIP
entities.text: The Hearthcircle is the ruling group, placed by talent, never by birth. The Elderhold is five halfling Elders who vote (Wendeline Brackenford, Fenwick Larkspur, Bertram Quillby, Ysolde Ambergate, Clementine Rook) plus Osric, their non-voting spokesperson and Leader. Bertram and Ysolde are secretly corrupt. Bertram's ledgers make tithe skimming vanish on paper, Ysolde steers bigger harvest shares to favored crop workers, and together they steer favorites into easier jobs. Osric suspects but can't prove it, and he hides a surname tied to someone high in the Kingdom. Osric (halfling, 142) rose from near-peasant through the Guard and the Hearthcircle; warm in public, very calculating underneath. He and Hesketh came up through the Guard in the same years on opposite shifts. A Hearthcircle member rises to the Elderhold only when a seat opens, by vote. The Hearthcircle is richer, trades with the merchants most and buys its fine metalwork from the capital.

entities.name: PEOPLE
entities.text: Tobin Ashby (halfling, 33, blacksmith's apprentice; determined, loyal, efficient). Doric (halfling, 67, strict, proud master smith; stung that the Hearthcircle buys its fine metalwork from the capital, not him). Murrow (artificer over 550 years old, race unknown, hidden under a deep hood; cold and businesslike, never mean; fears the Kingdom; his shop Monstradius is his workshop, and his ordinary-looking home in the NW housing district, three blocks away, is known to no one; he can cast a time-limited Nondetection-style spell and is researching an item that lasts; he was likely around when the well died and won't speak of it; Doric is an acquaintance; he has a soft spot for one kind of person, still undecided). Hesketh Reeve (human, 48, Guard Captain, picked from the ranks for his prowess; harsh but fair, not corrupt; a human over a mostly halfling Guard is part of the village's built-in bias). Elders: Wendeline (149, eldest, keeper of customs), Fenwick (145, ex-Guard, blunt, respects Hesketh), Bertram (138, keeps the ledgers and tithe counts), Ysolde (133, harvest stores and rationing, charming), Clementine (131, newest, curious about magic, deals with Murrow). Burn (human, about 45, short, big mustache, red cap; the Wellhouse's longtime regular, named for the one-line roasts he drops from his bar stool, only when something's actually funny, always about what someone said or did, never who they are; the Wellhouse elves' one friend; swears red-capped forest mushrooms make you grow; a little fire magic, enough to light a pipe; came down the Woodland Road with the merchants about 15 years ago and nobody knows his real name; SECRET: a court jester from the Kingdom's capital who fled after a joke landed on the wrong noble).

entities.name: BEYOND
entities.text: The Monster Wood (goblins, plus trolls and large beasts native to its deep woods; tall monsters and floating ones shaped the walls and the archers, and true flyers are rare) lies to the west, filling the land between the Kingdom and the croplands and running south into the mountains. An old blight is spreading through its deep woods, driving desperate goblins to raid Stoutwell's crops. Past the wood is a corrupt Kingdom and its capital, where the gloomy rock gnome artificer Glumtom works for the Kingdom, unwillingly: he heals, builds and raises the dead to labor, but never fights. He is distant family to Murrow. A tinkerer since childhood who ran a repair workshop, he was drafted as a registered Kingdom citizen and works only for them, in his cluttered workshop in the capital, for high pay that funds his reanimation research. He heals their guards, builds their tools and weapons, labors, and raises a few undead to build walls and buildings. He comes across as gloomy and keeps to himself. He made the Seeker's Lodestone, which the Kingdom doesn't know exists; he could find Murrow with it but isn't looking, and Murrow doesn't know of it. GuildScribe is the Kingdom's adventurers' guild hall in the capital (none exists in Stoutwell), named for its guildscribes, the clerks who keep its records: a parchment for each adventurer (race, trade, deeds, rank), registered companies (parties), the Archives (a library of spells, items, rules and monster lore), a bounty board and bestiary paying in gold, silver and copper, and an arena for sanctioned duels. It serves the Kingdom first. Guild members are on the Kingdom's books and can be drafted, and a seasonal census puts everyone else in the draft pool too. A few adventurers hunt the Monster Wood from the west, but none have made it past the blighted goblin lands, so none have reached Stoutwell. The deep woods' large beasts are hollowstags (stags nearly fifteen feet tall whose hollow antlers whistle as they run), rootwyrms (serpents as thick as a mill wheel, forced up as the Blight kills the roots they live in) and the ancient Mosswarden, so old a small forest grows on its back. The Blight is pushing them, thornback boars and floating driftmaws west toward the Kingdom, and gloamowls, dog-sized dusk owls, are among the wood's few true flyers. GuildScribe has posted bounties, but no one has yet brought back proof of the deep woods' beasts. Its senior guildscribe, the Scribe, is sour and unimpressed but secretly cares; anyone who tries to rob her is fined into the hall's swear jar. Threadbare peddlers (Tansy Ninefingers, Pruneface Yorik, Old Corrin, Widow Hesk and many more) take turns at an open stall in the capital's market and haggle hard. The Wandering Clerk, a guildscribe who broke from the hall, keeps a ledger of their own on the Kingdom's roads, swearing in adventurers where there's no guild; that road could bring the first guild ledger to Stoutwell. The Clerk and some of the peddlers (Wobble, Pruneface Yorik, Tansy Ninefingers, Old Corrin, Tam Pockets, Squint, Nan Gullyfoot, Kettle, Sella Windrags) follow the Clerk's road out to the Kingdom's edge and sometimes down the Woodland Road with the merchants as far as Stoutwell; the rest live in the capital. None of GuildScribe's people live in Stoutwell. GuildScribe's registered adventurers, ranked Novice, Journeyman, Seasoned or Veteran by their parchments, are a wider mix of peoples than Stoutwell sees (dwarves, drow, half-orcs, dragonborn, tieflings). Veterans include Sun (high elf monk), MuzzledKitty (tiefling wizard) and Blackass (dragonborn druid) of the company Science Club; Xan (tiefling druid) of Nuthaus; nobody (mountain dwarf barbarian) and Momma_Enya (dragonborn warlock) of No Trolls Here; Fel (drow fighter) of the Dweebs; Stabitha (human rogue) and nogood59 (gnome cleric). Others include Shadowflame, Briarpike, Mistkettle, Grimknot, Quack, Ryos, Moonkettle, Cinderfoot, Conanski, Ironmantle, Bramthistle, Mistcrest, Hawkthistle, Thunderwing and Bramblehelm. They hunt bounties across the Kingdom; none has reached Stoutwell. Some peddler relics may come from the Monster Wood. Merchants with escorts and a tax representative travel the Woodland Road, which is relatively safe but still dangerous. The tax representative is chosen for minimal bias, though the Kingdom's corruption can still creep in. Somewhere far past the Kingdom stands a divination tower; little is known of it.

entities.name: KINGDOM
entities.text: The Kingdom runs on paper. Its rolls (census, tax, the draft list, the register of artificers, GuildScribe's parchments) are kept in the Rolls House beside the Crown's seat in the capital, and its corruption is mostly about whose names get written, lost or moved for a bribe. The monarch is a distant banner; a handful of great houses hold the offices that matter (keeper of the rolls, master of the mint, warden of the roads, master of the draft) and pass them down like property. Osric's hidden surname may belong to one of them. House Harrowmere holds the Highwrit, the court office whose clerks copy, polish and seal every decree, writ and letter of the Crown and the Rolls House; its seal makes a document look right but never checks that it's true. Registered citizens get the Kingdom's law, its markets and bounty coin, and can be drafted for garrisons, labor or a rare skill. Every artificer the Kingdom finds goes into the register and is put to work, the way Glumtom was, which is exactly what Murrow fears. Enchanted items made in the Kingdom carry a registered artificer's mark; unmarked ones raise questions. Stoutwell has never been counted: the census stops at the Monster Wood, and the village pays its tax as one lump sum carried home by the tax representative, which is why no one there has been drafted and why a single guild ledger could end the deal. The capital is a walled city west of the Monster Wood, at the far end of the Woodland Road and the Clerk's road, ringed by the heartland's farms and river towns (grain, wool, timber; coin is minted in the capital). Inside are the Crown's seat, the Rolls House, the mint, the workshop quarter that makes the Hearthcircle's fine metalwork, GuildScribe's hall and arena, the market square and Glumtom's workshop; the poor quarters sit outside the old wall, where newer walls, some built by Glumtom's undead, are still going up. Towns and waystations grow poorer and less watched to the east; merchants hire escorts at the last waystation, where the Woodland Road leaves for Stoutwell. The Kingdom grew outward from the capital over centuries and stopped at the wood. Most of its people are human, with halflings and gnomes common in the towns; the capital draws everyone.

entities.name: OTHER WORLDS
entities.text: Arandur, an elf ranger and pickpocket from another world, was pulled out of it into another. In his youth, a rift dropped him in a village near Stoutwell (name not yet known). He was raised in a forest cabin by his hunter mother Silwen, who vanished with his distant father Faelan; he suspects a voiceless spectre that taught him to track is Silwen. Abandoned, he became a thief and a self-taught archer. He hides everything under contempt and silence, talks down magic, and fears trolls but can't fully hate them.

entities.name: WELLHOUSE
entities.text: The Wellhouse family are elves who moved here centuries ago for their soft spot for sharing and caring, and do nothing for the village beyond the tavern. They have a few children but don’t make many—they don’t want trouble. Their name is not yet known.

entities.name: MONSTER WOOD
entities.text: The wood is filled with goblins, plus trolls and large beasts native to its deep woods; tall monsters and floating ones shaped the walls and the archers, and true flyers are rare. A blight is spreading through its deep woods, driving desperate goblins to raid Stoutwell's crops. GuildScribe has posted bounties, but no one has yet brought back proof of the deep woods’ beasts.  The rootwyrms have been driven out by the Blight and they aren't returning; their remains now feed giant fungi growing in the darkest parts of the forest.

entities.name: MAGIC
entities.text: Common but weak. It assists work, it doesn’t replace it. Types: elemental (wind, fire, earth), strength enhancement, detection. Everyday uses include mending torn or cracked things and loosening or firming soil. Healing specialists are very rare and only ever human, from humans' affinity for it; a small or medium village may have 2 or 3 at a time (Stoutwell has 2). Healers use magic to assist the body's own healing. Artificers aren’t healers but can still heal, leaning on natural healing and on drawing other people’s healing magic, sometimes nefariously. A fire user who can boil a pot of water counts as super skilled. Everyone has a well of mana. It refills more slowly than the body heals, and there’s no visible bar. Running out (mana deprivation) causes sickness, dizziness or passing out. Fire is the opposite of cold, so a fire user low on mana grows cold, more so the emptier they are. Elves are most magical, then humans, then halflings. People can have latent magic they don’t know about. Objects hold mana but can’t make it. A charged item normally works only for the person whose mana is in it; a very rare ability, nearly as rare as artificing, lets an item work without its owner. Wind users are rare and far more often human. Strength enhancement is fairly common (Tobin uses it to hammer hot steel).

entities.name: ITEMS
entities.text: Hearthstones are charged river stones; the Truthglass is rare clear quartz; mirrorstone is rare black glass shaped by magic. Doric forges iron (Featherhook hooks to Murrow’s specifications, the Guard’s gear, ornate work) with a smith’s hammer. Timber comes from dead-tree runs, is cut at the lumber mill and stored in the lumber yard. A few short, twisted ash trees grow on the Ashen Reach; their dense, tough wood is too short for beams but prized by the woodworkers for tool handles, weapon hilts and arrow shafts. Leather comes from the herders' cattle, worked at the tannery, and clothes everyone. The grain mill grinds flour. The fishing settlement’s catch feeds Stoutwell. The halfling Guard fights behind big shields; human archers carry bows. Coin is gold, silver and copper; Murrow takes coin or barter on the same terms for everyone, and his rare items cost more than people expect. The Rift compass doesn’t point to a world: it shows how thick the rifts are nearby, and a needle twitching wildly means many unstable tears. It can’t tell you which world a rift leads to.

entities.name: ARTIFICERS
entities.text: Extremely rare. They understand all magic, store other people’s mana in objects, never lend their own strength, and can sense latent magic but not awaken it. Murrow's Elemental Test: shown an array of items (a stone, a feather), an injured child he’s healing is drawn to the one their secretly drawn mana reacts in, revealing their element; most people find their element on their own. A secret artificer item, the Seeker’s Lodestone (a round, flat disc of mirrorstone, a rare black glass), can locate other artificers. entities.name: RACES
entities.text: Halflings are stout, thick-skinned and naturally heat-resistant (well suited to smithing), quick, quiet and lucky, and homebodies who love good food and a warm hearth. They reach adulthood around 20, live to about 150 and have children less often, so the oldest villagers are almost always halflings and the shortest in any crowd. Humans rarely pass 100; they’re leaner, more attuned to elemental magic, and do about 70% of the wood chopping. Elves exist as the Wellhouse family, but their origin is unknown - they arrived centuries ago for their soft spot for sharing and caring, and do nothing for the village beyond the tavern. Their name is not yet known.

entities.name: The Universe: The Grand Orrery

fields.scope: A universe of several worlds that can tie together. Most of this draft takes place on one of them, Verrowen, centered on the walled village of Stoutwell.
fields.linked_worlds: The worlds connect through **rifts**, random tears that open and close and pull in people, monsters or even whole buildings. That's why the same monsters turn up on different worlds. Arandur, an elf thief, was pulled out of his own world into another (see Characters from Other Worlds).
fields.doorway_rifts: Some artificers can open rifts on purpose, using a doorway as their boundary for the magic.

entities.body:
An orrery is a clockwork model of the heavens. **The Grand Orrery** is the artificers' name for the universe, picturing its worlds as moving parts in one great mechanism. Only high-ranking and learned people, those with a wide enough view to name more than their own world, know it. Most people, Stoutwell's villagers included, have never heard the name.

**The world of Verrowen:** Stoutwell's world is called **Verrowen**. It's a scholarly name, recorded in books. Small villages own only a few books, and only kingdoms keep libraries, so most common folk simply call it "the world" or "the land."

- **Scope:** A universe of several worlds that can tie together. Most of this draft takes place on one of them, Verrowen, centered on the walled village of Stoutwell.
- **Tone:** Medieval fantasy, with D&D-style monsters.
- **Linked worlds:** The worlds connect through **rifts**, random tears that open and close and pull in people, monsters or even whole buildings. That's why the same monsters turn up on different worlds. Arandur, an elf thief, was pulled out of his own world into another (see Characters from Other Worlds).
- **Doorway rifts:** Some artificers can open rifts on purpose, using a doorway as their boundary for the magic.

entities.name: How Magic Works
entities.body: Magic is everywhere, but it's small. It helps people work. It doesn't do the work for them.

entities.name: The core rules
entities.body:
1. **Common but weak:** Almost everyone has a little magic. Very few have a lot.
2. **It assists, it doesn't do:** A fire user can light the stove, but someone still has to cook.
3. **A low ceiling:** A fire user who can boil a pot of water is considered super skilled.
4. **Types:** Everyday magic is elemental: wind, fire or earth. Strength enhancement is a fairly common non-elemental ability, used for anything from hammering hot steel to heavy lifting. Detection magic also exists.
5. **By race:** Elves are the most magical, then humans, then halflings. Humans are more attuned to elemental magic, and wind users, though rare, are far more likely to be human.
6. **Latent magic:** People can have abilities they don't know they have.
7. **Everyday uses:** Mending torn clothes, cracked pots or a nicked shield (maybe a halfling specialty), and earth magic that loosens soil for planting or firms up a muddy path.

entities.name: Healers

fields.very_rare_and_only_human: Healing specialists come strictly from the human race, because of humans' affinity for it.
fields.how_many: A small or medium village may have 2 or 3 at a time. Stoutwell has two.
fields.how_they_heal: Their magic helps the body heal itself. It doesn't replace natural healing.
fields.artificers: They aren't healers, but they can still heal. That's how Murrow and Glumtom do it. Artificers lean on natural healing and on using other people's healing magic, often more nefariously.

entities.body:
- **Very rare, and only human:** Healing specialists come strictly from the human race, because of humans' affinity for it.
- **How many:** A small or medium village may have 2 or 3 at a time. Stoutwell has two.
- **How they heal:** Their magic helps the body heal itself. It doesn't replace natural healing.
- **Artificers:** They aren't healers, but they can still heal. That's how Murrow and Glumtom do it. Artificers lean on natural healing and on using other people's healing magic, often more nefariously.

entities.name: Mana

fields.mana_deprivation: Running out makes a person sick and dizzy, and can make them pass out.
fields.fire_mana_and_cold: Fire is the opposite of cold, so a fire user who runs low on mana grows cold. The emptier their well, the deeper the chill.

entities.body:
- Nearly everyone has a personal well of **mana** (MP) that fuels their magic.
- Mana refills over time, more slowly than the body heals naturally.
- There's no visible bar or number. People simply feel how much they have left.
- **Mana deprivation:** Running out makes a person sick and dizzy, and can make them pass out.
- **Fire mana and cold:** Fire is the opposite of cold, so a fire user who runs low on mana grows cold. The emptier their well, the deeper the chill.

entities.name: Artificers and enchanted items

fields.attunement: An item charged with someone's mana normally only works for that person. A very rare ability, almost as rare as being an artificer, lets an item work without its owner present.
fields.no_awakening: An artificer can sense latent magic but can't awaken it.

entities.body:
- **Objects hold magic, they don't make it.** An artificer can take a person's mana and store it inside an object. A stone charged with a fire user's mana warms when fire is cast on it, burning through that supply until it's gone.
- **Attunement:** An item charged with someone's mana normally only works for that person. A very rare ability, almost as rare as being an artificer, lets an item work without its owner present.
- **Artificers** understand every type of magic, even the ones they can't cast. They never lend their own strength. They only let people use their own abilities, whether or not those people know they have them.
- **No awakening:** An artificer can sense latent magic but can't awaken it.

entities.name: The Elemental Test
entities.body:
A quiet way to find a child's element before they know it themselves:

1. The child is shown an array of items, such as a stone or a feather.
2. Without a word, the artificer draws a little of the child's mana into an item. The child doesn't know it's happening.
3. The child is naturally drawn to the item they can use, and its reaction reveals their element. A stone that turns weightless means wind.

entities.name: Stoutwell
entities.body: A small, self-sufficient walled village of simple wooden homes, about **600 years old**. Its people live off the land and make what they need.

entities.name: The people

fields.halflings_and_humans: Roughly 72% human (about 158) and 28% halfling (about 62). Halflings reach adulthood around 20 and live to about 150, while humans rarely pass 100, meaning halflings have fewer children and are shorter than humans.
fields.elves: The Wellhouse family, the only elves in the village. They keep to the tavern and are generally ostracized.
fields.halflings: Short, stout and tougher than they look, with thick skin and natural heat resistance. They're homebodies at heart who love good food and a warm hearth, but they're quick, quiet and lucky when it counts.
fields.work_and_gender: Heavy manual work like smithing tends to fall to men because of muscle mass. That's a tendency, not a rule. Nothing is formally restricted.

entities.body:
- **Population:** about 220
- **Halflings and humans:** Roughly 72% human (about 158) and 28% halfling (about 62). Halflings reach adulthood around 20 and live to about 150, while humans rarely pass 100, meaning halflings have fewer children and are shorter than humans.
- **Elves:** The Wellhouse family, the only elves in the village. They keep to the tavern and are generally ostracized.
- **Halflings:** Short, stout and tougher than they look, with thick skin and natural heat resistance. They're homebodies at heart who love good food and a warm hearth, but they're quick, quiet and lucky when it counts.
- **Work and gender:** Heavy manual work like smithing tends to fall to men because of muscle mass. That's a tendency, not a rule. Nothing is formally restricted.

entities.name: What Stoutwell is known for

fields.the_ale: A local stout that has never lost its potency. Human gatherers specialize in collecting its ingredients. For centuries the supply has been tightly restricted by the lack of water.
fields.the_smithing: Stoutwell's smiths are known for ornate work, alongside everyday tools and the Guard's gear.

entities.body:
Unofficially, Stoutwell is known for its **ale** and its **blacksmithing**.

- **The ale:** A local stout that has never lost its potency. Human gatherers specialize in collecting its ingredients. For centuries the supply has been tightly restricted by the lack of water.
- **The smithing:** Stoutwell's smiths are known for ornate work, alongside everyday tools and the Guard's gear.

entities.name: The Wellhouse
entities.body:
- The village tavern and bar, serving the local stout.
- It's owned by the wealthy **Wellhouse** family, elves who came to Stoutwell centuries ago out of a soft spot for sharing and caring.
- They have economic ties to the farmers and gatherers who supply the brewing.
- Outside the tavern they want nothing to do with village work.

entities.name: Burn, the Wellhouse's regular

fields.who_he_is: A short, stout human man of about 45 with a big mustache and a battered red cap, so short he's often taken for a halfling. He's tired of being asked. Everyone calls him **Burn**, for his burns: the one-line roasts he drops from his stool at the Wellhouse bar. No one in Stoutwell knows his true name.
fields.how_he_got_here: He came down the Woodland Road with the merchants about fifteen years ago, took a stool at the Wellhouse, and never left. He tells a different story about where he's from every time he's asked. He's one of the few outsiders who lives in Stoutwell.
fields.his_manner: Friendly, quick and dry, a little teasing, and never trying too hard. He's been there so long he knows every running joke. He only speaks up when something is actually funny. When he does, it's one line, built on the exact thing someone just said or did, and then he goes back to his stout. He never explains a joke and never tells two in a row.
fields.his_rules: He roasts what people say and do, never who they are: not their looks, their people, or their station. He only roasts what he saw or heard himself, and he never makes things up about anyone. Asked straight out who he really is, he won't lie; he makes a joke and changes the subject.
fields.the_wellhouses: He's the one regular who sits and talks with the Wellhouse elves as friends, and they've quietly let his tab run for years. He's warm under the teasing, and the village's mood about the elves is the one thing he's never joked about.
fields.mushrooms: He claims the red-capped mushrooms brought in by the gatherers can cause growth, though this is untrue. He continues to eat them regardless.
fields.magic: A little fire. With a snap of his fingers he can light a pipe, a candle or a wick, never more. He's nowhere near boiling a pot of water. On a night with too many snaps he gets cold and sits nearer the hearth.
fields.his_secret: He was a jester at court in the Kingdom's capital until a joke landed on the wrong noble. He ran down the Woodland Road before they could find out where he'd gone, and he's been hiding in Stoutwell ever since.
fields.story_hooks: A merchant or the tax representative on the Woodland Road could be someone who saw him at court. Having worked the capital's court, he may know Kingdom names that Stoutwell doesn't, maybe even the surname Osric hides.

entities.name: Water and the dead well

fields.the_name: Stoutwell was named for its central well, once the source of its famous ale.
fields.the_blight: About 550 years ago, the blight dried the well up.
fields.centuries_of_water_runs: Since then, villagers traveled in small groups to the river and hauled back enough water to refill the dry well for a couple of days at a time.
fields.irrigation: Recently, the artificer Murrow built an irrigation system that brings river water into the village. The river itself flows away from both the village and the woods.
fields.the_ale_maybe: More water could mean more ale for the first time in centuries. Whether it will, and what that would mean for the Wellhouses and whoever controls the supply, is still open.

entities.body:
- **The name:** Stoutwell was named for its central well, once the source of its famous ale.
- **The blight:** About 550 years ago, the blight dried the well up.
- **Centuries of water runs:** Since then, villagers traveled in small groups to the river and hauled back enough water to refill the dry well for a couple of days at a time.
- **Irrigation:** Recently, the artificer Murrow built an irrigation system that brings river water into the village. The river itself flows away from both the village and the woods.
- **The ale, maybe:** More water could mean more ale for the first time in centuries. Whether it will, and what that would mean for the Wellhouses and whoever controls the supply, is still open.

entities.name: Layout

fields.walls: Short, but substantial enough for most monsters
fields.gates: One in each wall: north, east, south and west.
fields.the_west_gate: The croplands, the Woodland Road and the Monster Wood all lie outside it. It's the busiest gate, the most dangerous, and the one goblin raiders hit hardest.
fields.the_south_side: The Ashen Reach, Stoutwell's training grounds, lies to the south. The slums run along the south wall, right beside it.
fields.why_the_slums_are_by_the_training_ground: Ash dust and the noise of the drills make the south wall the least wanted land in the village, so it's where poorer families could afford to live. The slums provided the majority of recruits for the Guard; trainee soldiers lived within walking distance of the training grounds.
fields.neighborhoods: The wealth gap shows on the map. There are slums, where poorer families live packed into plainer homes, and a nicer area of better-kept homes and shops.
fields.nw: The housing district. Middle- to upper-class homes, the Elderhold's included. The slums keep their own separate, poorer housing.
fields.ne: Monstradius, plus Murrow's irrigation and research building, set toward the village center.
fields.sw: The shopping district, on the nicer side but close to the slums. The Wellhouse stands in its northeast corner.
fields.se: The slums side, home to Doric's smithy.
fields.town_center: Just left of center are the dried well and the large Gathering Hall, where the Elderhold meets.
fields.the_divide: The line between the nicer area and the slums runs on a slant, so the shopping district falls on the nicer side.

entities.name: History
entities.body:
- The Monster Wood had always been dangerous.
- The Monster Wood had always been dangerous. The founding stories were never passed down.

entities.name: Groups and jobs

fields.village_workers: Smiths, tanners, woodworkers and other trades inside the walls.
fields.herders: Cattle, raised for food and leather.
fields.farmers: The croplands outside the west gate, which take up the most land.
fields.gatherers: Firewood runs, foragers at the forest edge, and ingredients for the ale.

entities.body:
1. **Communal schooling:** The youngest children are taught together.
2. **Placement:** As they grow, the Elders place each villager into a group based on what they're physically suited for. It's meant to be fairly unbiased.
3. **A job within the group:** Each person is given a specific role.
4. **Freedom to switch:** No one is locked in. Someone who is bad at their job can move to another of their choice, within reason.

**The groups:**

- **Village Workers:** Smiths, tanners, woodworkers and other trades inside the walls.
- **Herders:** Cattle, raised for food and leather.
- **Farmers:** The croplands outside the west gate, which take up the most land.
- **Gatherers:** Firewood runs, foragers at the forest edge, and ingredients for the ale.
- **The Guard:** The full-time defenders.
- **The Hearthcircle:** The ruling group.

entities.name: Trades

fields.ash_wood: A few short, twisted ash trees grow on the Ashen Reach. Their wood is too short for beams, so timber still comes from the dead-tree runs, but it's dense and tough, and the woodworkers prize it for tool handles, weapon hilts and arrow shafts.
fields.the_elders_scenic_cows: A couple of cows kept just to be looked at, which is a rare luxury.
fields.lumber_mill: Cuts timber into boards and beams.
fields.lumber_yard: It supplies the materials for the village's wooden homes and construction. Between this and the Featherhooks, Stoutwell is more advanced than its size suggests.

entities.body:
- **Blacksmith:** Doric and his apprentice, Tobin.
- **Tannery:** Leather for clothing.
- **Woodworkers:** Weapon hilts and ornate structures.
- **Ash wood:** A few short, twisted ash trees grow on the Ashen Reach. Their wood is too short for beams, so timber still comes from the dead-tree runs, but it's dense and tough, and the woodworkers prize it for tool handles, weapon hilts and arrow shafts.
- **Farmers and herders:** Crops and cattle.
- **The Elders' scenic cows:** A couple of cows kept just to be looked at, which is a rare luxury.

**Mills and the lumber yard:**

- **Grain mill:** Grinds the harvest into flour.
- **Lumber mill:** Cuts timber into boards and beams.
- **Lumber yard:** It supplies the materials for the village's wooden homes and construction. Between this and the Featherhooks, Stoutwell is more advanced than its size suggests.
- **The millers:** Among the village's wealthier families.

**Where they are:** The mills stand outside the walls on the river to the east, powered by its current. That's opposite the Monster Wood, but still a post the Guard has to cover. The lumber yard is inside the walls near the east gate.

entities.name: Firewood and daily magic

fields.chopping: Humans do about 70% of it. They're leaner and have to work longer to keep up. Stout halflings handle the other 30%.
fields.dead_tree_runs: One or two villagers use detection magic to find fallen trees near the forest edge. A group drags them back while wind users lighten the load and cushion it from below. A Guard escort of a couple of shield-bearers and an archer or two goes along.
fields.foraging: A small group gathers edible crops from the forest edge.

entities.body:
- Homes are heated by wood stoves, so firewood is constant work.
- **Chopping:** Humans do about 70% of it. They're leaner and have to work longer to keep up. Stout halflings handle the other 30%.
- **Dead-tree runs:** One or two villagers use detection magic to find fallen trees near the forest edge. A group drags them back while wind users lighten the load and cushion it from below. A Guard escort of a couple of shield-bearers and an archer or two goes along.
- **Foraging:** A small group gathers edible crops from the forest edge.

entities.name: The Guard

fields.shield_bearers: Stout halflings fighting from behind big shields they can almost fully hide behind.
fields.archers: Humans on the walls who shoot down floating monsters and the rare flyer.
fields.full_time_guards: Both men and women. The only requirement is strength.
fields.the_rotation: Villagers serve a couple of days a month, rotating between inside the village, the croplands, the walls, and escorting gatherers.
fields.strain: With so few halflings, the shield Guard is small and overworked. Stress and defiance run high, but extreme punishments keep it to a little skimming and some shift dodging.
fields.funding: The Guard is paid for communally through the guard tithe. Each household gives a share of its harvest, crafts or labor to keep the Guard fed, armed and paid. Wealthier families, such as the millers, give more, better quality, or both.

entities.body:
- **Shield-bearers:** Stout halflings fighting from behind big shields they can almost fully hide behind.
- **Archers:** Humans on the walls who shoot down floating monsters and the rare flyer.
- **Full-time guards:** Both men and women. The only requirement is strength.

entities.name: Law and punishment

fields.punishments: Depending on the crime, from the stocks and floggings to exile and even execution.
fields.weregild: Payment can be accepted in place of punishment.

entities.body:
- **Punishments:** Depending on the crime, from the stocks and floggings to exile and even execution.
- **Weregild:** Payment can be accepted in place of punishment.

entities.name: Leadership

fields.the_hearthcircle: The ruling group, something like a royal family. Talented villagers are placed into it, never by birth. That allows some bias, and some corruption.
fields.the_elderhold: The Leader and five Elders, the ones who rose to the top of the Hearthcircle.
fields.the_elders: Five votes, an odd number so there are no ties. They work together to advise the Leader, focused on research, survival and peace. Their focuses separate naturally, without formal titles.
fields.the_leader: Doesn't vote. He's the translator and spokesperson for the Elders.
fields.getting_a_seat: A Hearthcircle member rises to the Elderhold only when a seat opens, and then by vote.
fields.why_the_elders_are_halflings: The oldest villagers in physical years are almost always halflings.

entities.body:
Stoutwell is a village, not a kingdom, so it has no king.

- **The Hearthcircle:** The ruling group, something like a royal family. Talented villagers are placed into it, never by birth. That allows some bias, and some corruption.
- **The Elderhold:** The Leader and five Elders, the ones who rose to the top of the Hearthcircle.
- **The Elders:** Five votes, an odd number so there are no ties. They work together to advise the Leader, focused on research, survival and peace. Their focuses separate naturally, without formal titles.
- **The Leader:** Doesn't vote. He's the translator and spokesperson for the Elders.
- **Getting a seat:** A Hearthcircle member rises to the Elderhold only when a seat opens, and then by vote.
- **Why the Elders are halflings:** The oldest villagers in physical years are almost always halflings.

entities.name: Corruption
entities.body:
The corruption comes from the Elderhold. Two of the five Elders currently work together to commit it:

- Favorites get placed into easier jobs.
- Favored crop workers get bigger harvest shares.
- Skimming from the guard tithe goes unpunished.

entities.name: Tobin Ashby

fields.role: Blacksmith's apprentice. He was born into a smithing family, and the Elders placed him at the forge.
fields.magic: Minimal. He uses a strength enhancement to hammer hot steel harder.
fields.where_his_story_is_heading: The goblin raids aren't random. He follows the trail back toward the Blight, and to whoever, or whatever, is behind it.

entities.body:
- **Male halfling, 33.** Young but fully grown for a halfling.
- **Role:** Blacksmith's apprentice. He was born into a smithing family, and the Elders placed him at the forge.
- **Personality:** Determined, loyal and efficient.
- **Magic:** Minimal. He uses a strength enhancement to hammer hot steel harder.
- **Where his story is heading:** The goblin raids aren't random. He follows the trail back toward the Blight, and to whoever, or whatever, is behind it.

entities.name: Doric

fields.personality: Strict because he hates mistakes, and deeply proud of his work.
fields.standing: He isn't in the Hearthcircle, but he advises them on metalwork. They respect him but don't rely on him.
fields.sore_spot: The Hearthcircle orders its fine metalwork from the capital instead of from him, and for a smith this proud, it stings.
fields.on_tobin: Talented, but not ready to take over.
fields.murrow: They're acquaintances. Doric forges the iron for Murrow's Featherhooks.

entities.body:
- **Male halfling, 67,** in the younger part of his prime.
- **Role:** Master blacksmith and Tobin's master.
- **Personality:** Strict because he hates mistakes, and deeply proud of his work.
- **Standing:** He isn't in the Hearthcircle, but he advises them on metalwork. They respect him but don't rely on him.
- **Sore spot:** The Hearthcircle orders its fine metalwork from the capital instead of from him, and for a smith this proud, it stings.
- **On Tobin:** Talented, but not ready to take over.
- **Murrow:** They're acquaintances. Doric forges the iron for Murrow's Featherhooks.

entities.name: Osric, Leader of the Elderhold
entities.secret: His real surname, which he keeps hidden, ties him to someone high up in the Kingdom. Almost no one else knows.

fields.background: He came up from near the bottom, close to peasant. He worked his way into the Guard, then the Hearthcircle, then the Elderhold. Respect made him Leader. He rose mostly fairly, with perhaps a favor or two called in.
fields.underneath: Very calculating, well educated, and careful with every word.
fields.the_corruption: He's not part of it. He suspects it but has no proof, so in practice he lets it continue.

entities.body:
- **Male halfling, 142.** That's within the Elders' age range but younger than the eldest, which keeps him in touch with the present.
- **Background:** He came up from near the bottom, close to peasant. He worked his way into the Guard, then the Hearthcircle, then the Elderhold. Respect made him Leader. He rose mostly fairly, with perhaps a favor or two called in.
- **Public face:** Warm and well-liked.
- **Underneath:** Very calculating, well educated, and careful with every word.
- **The corruption:** He's not part of it. He suspects it but has no proof, so in practice he lets it continue.
- **Secret:** His real surname, which he keeps hidden, ties him to someone high up in the Kingdom. Almost no one else knows.

entities.name: The Elders
entities.body:
All five are halflings.

| Elder | Age | Leans toward | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Wendeline Brackenford** (F) | 149 | Peace | The eldest. Keeper of customs. Gentle but stubborn. |
| **Fenwick Larkspur** (M) | 145 | Survival | Ex-Guard. Blunt and practical. Respects Hesketh. |
| **Bertram Quillby** (M) | 138 | Research | Keeps the records, ledgers and tithe counts. Precise and polite. **Corrupt.** |
| **Ysolde Ambergate** (F) | 133 | Survival | Oversees harvest stores and rationing. Charming and persuasive. **Corrupt.** |
| **Clementine Rook** (F) | 131 | Research | The newest Elder. Curious about magic, and the one who deals with Murrow. |

**The corrupt pair:** Bertram's ledgers make the skimming vanish on paper, and Ysolde steers the harvest shares. Together they shape placements.

entities.name: Murrow's items

fields.hearthstones: Smooth river stones charged by a fire user in Murrow's shop, set to release slowly so a stove stays warm through the night. One night per charge, and they still need embers: they warm a fire but don't replace it. Rare and expensive.
fields.featherhooks: Iron hooks forged by Doric and imprinted by Murrow with a wind pattern. They cut a log's weight about in half while it's dragged, drawing on the holder's latent wind, so they work better for humans than halflings. Holding one too long leaves you winded.
fields.wardbells: Bells on the walls with a detection user's sense set into the metal, pointed at the Monster Wood. They ring on their own when something large comes out, but can't tell goblins from trolls, only big from small, and need a detection user to refresh them every few weeks.
fields.truthglass: A rare piece of clear quartz charged with detection magic. It shows whether a coin, seal or signed paper is real, but only answers real or fake, never who forged it or why. Dangerous for anyone skimming the guard tithe, or for a crooked tax representative.
fields.the_rift_compass: A secret project, about 80% complete. It points toward places where the worlds are thin. How it works is unknown even to Murrow, and it may use a kind of magic nobody in the village has.
fields.a_lasting_hiding_charm_research: His spell that hides him from magical detection wears off. He's working on an item that would hold it for good. It isn't made yet.

entities.name: The Monster Wood

fields.goblin_raiders: The main threat. They raid the croplands outside the walls.
fields.trolls: They're natural to the deep woods, the same kind of creature as in Arandur's world. The village's defenses keep them from being a problem.
fields.large_beasts: They live in the deep woods. The ones known so far are **hollowstags** (stags nearly fifteen feet tall at the antlers, whose hollow antlers whistle as they run), **rootwyrms** (serpents as thick as a mill wheel that live in the roots under the deep woods) and the ancient **Mosswarden**, a beast so old a small forest grows on its back. Their stat lines are in [`bestiary.md`](bestiary.md).
fields.tall_and_floating_monsters: These shaped the walls and the archers. Hollowstags are the tall kind; **driftmaws**, cart-sized gasbags that drift above the canopy trailing sticky tendrils, are the floating kind. True flyers are rare; the **gloamowl**, a dog-sized owl that hunts at dusk, is one of the few.
fields.driven_out_by_the_blight: As the Blight kills the roots and dries the ground, it's pushing the deep woods' creatures, **thornback boars** among them, out toward the edges and west toward the Kingdom.

- **Driven out by the Blight:** As the Blight kills the roots and dries the ground, it's pushing the deep woods' creatures, **thornback boars** among them, out toward the edges and west toward the Kingdom.

entities.name: The Blight
entities.body:
- An old blight that has been eating through the deep woods for at least 550 years. It's what killed Stoutwell's well.
- It has finally reached the goblins' part of the forest. They're fleeing it, desperate for a safe place. They can't get past the walls, so they raid the fields for food and survival.
- Its origins remain shrouded in mystery, though some whisper of an ancient artificer's experiment gone awry.

entities.name: Beyond the Village

fields.the_kingdom: A real kingdom farther off, past the woods. Stoutwell sits on its far edge. Like any kingdom, it carries moral corruption and the cruelty that comes with power. The full notes are in [`working-notes.md`](working-notes.md) under Beyond the Village.
fields.the_kingdom_runs_on_paper: Its power is its rolls: the census, the tax rolls, the draft list, the register of artificers and GuildScribe's parchments, all kept in the **Rolls House** beside the Crown's seat. A name on paper can be taxed, drafted, fined or found. Its corruption is mostly about whose names get written, lost or moved.
fields.the_crown_and_the_great_houses: The monarch is a distant banner. A handful of noble houses hold the offices that matter (keeper of the rolls, master of the mint, warden of the roads, master of the draft) and pass them down like property. Osric's hidden surname could belong to one of them.
fields.the_highwrit: The court office whose clerks copy, polish and proofread the decrees, writs and letters of the Crown and the Rolls House. Nothing leaves the court without its seal. **House Harrowmere** holds it and passes it down. It makes a document look right; it never checks that it's true, and a Truthglass can tell whether the seal is real, not whether the words under it are honest.
fields.the_draft_and_the_register: Registered citizens get the Kingdom's law, its markets and bounty coin, and can be drafted. Every artificer the Kingdom finds is written into the register and put to work, the way Glumtom was. Enchanted items made in the Kingdom carry a registered artificer's mark.
fields.the_deal_at_the_edge: The census stops at the Monster Wood. Stoutwell pays its Kingdom tax as one lump sum through the tax representative instead of being counted name by name, so no one there has ever been drafted, and Murrow can live there unregistered. One guild ledger could end the arrangement.
fields.the_capital_and_the_heartland: The capital is a walled city west of the Monster Wood, at the far end of the Woodland Road and the Clerk's road. Around it lies the heartland's farmland and river towns, the source of grain, wool and timber; coin is minted in the capital. Inside are the Crown's seat and the Rolls House, the mint, the workshop quarter where the Hearthcircle's fine metalwork is made, GuildScribe's hall and arena, the market square with the peddlers' stall, and Glumtom's workshop. The poor quarters sit outside the old wall, where newer walls, some built by Glumtom's undead, are still going up. Eastward, the towns and waystations grow poorer and less watched. Merchants hire their escorts at the last waystation, where the Woodland Road leaves for Stoutwell.
fields.peoples: Most of the Kingdom is human, with halflings and gnomes common in the towns. The capital draws everyone, including the dwarves, drow, half-orcs, dragonborn and tieflings on GuildScribe's parchments.
fields.history: The Kingdom grew outward from the capital over centuries, writing each new town into its rolls, until it reached the Monster Wood and stopped, because the wood was cheaper to tax around than to cross.
fields.the_woodland_road: A path through the woods, outside the west gate, to the Kingdom. It's relatively safe, but still dangerous.
fields.merchants: Traders travel the road with safety escorts, so the village isn't cut off. The wealthier Hearthcircle trades with them most and gets the best goods, including most of its fine metalwork, from the Kingdom's capital.
fields.the_tax_representative: Travels with the merchants to collect the Kingdom's tax. The role is chosen carefully to keep bias low, but the Kingdom's corruption can still creep in.
fields.the_lake: The river flows south past the mills and opens into a lake at its southern end, southeast of Stoutwell.
fields.the_mountain_wall: An impassable wall of mountains runs along the east and turns west along the south, and the lake lies in its corner. No one goes over it. Its southern arm runs past the Ashen Reach, so the training grounds sit between the village and the mountains.
fields.the_fishing_settlement: A small fishing settlement on the lake's far shore, across the water from Stoutwell, at the foot of the mountains. Usually only 5 to 10 people live there. They fish, and they aren't part of the village, but their catch is a source of food for Stoutwell. Its name isn't decided yet.
fields.the_hidden_pass_secret: The fishers secretly guard and hide a passage through the mountains. It leads to somewhere on the other side that no one in Stoutwell knows of. What's there is still to be decided.
fields.the_ashen_reach: A plain of grey soil to the south of Stoutwell where nothing grows tall. It's the village's training grounds. The slums along the south wall sit right beside it: the ash and noise keep land there cheap, and the slums supply most of the Guard's recruits. A few short, twisted ash trees grow there. Some say it's an old battlefield, others that a past Grand Orrery event touched down there.
fields.the_divination_tower: A tower somewhere past the Kingdom, farther off than anywhere Stoutwell knows. Who keeps it, and what it sees, is still to be decided.

entities.name: GuildScribe, the Kingdom's guild hall

fields.what_it_is: The adventurers' guild hall in the Kingdom's capital. It's named for its **guildscribes**, the clerks who keep every record the hall runs on. There's nothing like it in Stoutwell. A village that small has the Guard, not a guild.
fields.the_parchment: Every adventurer who joins is written onto a parchment: name, race, trade, level of skill and deeds. Their rank in the hall rises as the parchment fills.
fields.companies: Adventurers register in companies, small parties that take work together under one name.
fields.the_archives: The guild's library of spells, items, rules and monster lore. It's one of the few places in Verrowen where that knowledge is written down.
fields.the_bounty_board: Monster bounties, paid in Kingdom coin (gold, silver and copper). The guildscribes keep a bestiary of every creature a bounty has been posted for.
fields.the_arena: Sanctioned duels between members, for coin and standing.
fields.the_kingdoms_hand: The hall serves the Kingdom first. Its records and its corruption both belong to the Kingdom.
fields.the_draft_pool: Joining the guild puts your name on the Kingdom's books, and registered citizens can be drafted. A census every season catches everyone who never joined, so they end up in the draft pool too.
fields.adventurers_in_the_wood: Only a few adventurers hunt the Monster Wood, coming in from the west on the Kingdom's side. None have made it past the blighted section where the goblins live, so none have reached Stoutwell.
fields.the_bestiarys_blank_page: GuildScribe has posted bounties for the beasts the Blight is driving out, but no one has ever brought back proof of the deep woods' great beasts. The first company to return with a hollowstag antler would make its name.

entities.name: The Scribe, the peddlers and the Wandering Clerk

fields.the_scribe: GuildScribe's senior guildscribe, who answers adventurers at the desk. Sour, unimpressed and always comparing things to how they were done in her day, she scolds young adventurers for not eating enough. She secretly cares a little, and would never admit it. Anyone who tries to rob her is fined into the hall's swear jar.
fields.the_peddlers: Threadbare traders who take turns at an open stall in the capital's market square. They haggle hard and sell odd, mostly honest wares. Now and then one turns up a real relic and can't say where it came from. (Fenwick Loose-Coin and Widow Hesk are no relation to Fenwick Larkspur or Hesketh Reeve.)
fields.the_wandering_clerk: A guildscribe who broke from the hall and keeps a ledger of their own on the Kingdom's roads, swearing in adventurers where there's no guild, posting bounties and sending them to the nearest peddler's stall. Some of the peddlers follow the Clerk's road.
fields.the_first_ledger_in_stoutwell: The Clerk's road, by way of the Woodland Road, could bring the first guild ledger to Stoutwell, putting villagers' names on paper the Kingdom might read.
fields.a_relic_from_the_wood: One of the peddlers' unexplained relics could have come out of the Monster Wood.

entities.name: Where GuildScribe's people live and travel

fields.the_scribe: An old human woman who lives in two rooms above the hall in the capital and has kept its desk longer than anyone can say. She hasn't left the capital in years and sees no reason to.

entities.name: The capital peddlers
entities.section: Beyond the Village › Where GuildScribe's people live and travel

fields.bregga_stumpteeth: Human, F. A broad, gap-toothed hawker whose voice carries across the whole square. Sells anything that can be sold by shouting.
fields.widow_hesk: Human, F. Has been "recently widowed" for as long as anyone has known her. Runs her pitch on sympathy and is very good at it.
fields.fenwick_loose_coin: Halfling, M. Always a copper short, and always sure the next sale will fix it. Owes a little to most of the other peddlers.
fields.marda_the_reformed_cutpurse: Human, F. A former pickpocket who went straight and won't let anyone forget it. Still checks every buyer's pockets with her eyes.
fields.grithnall_the_threadbare: Human, M. Lanky and patched from hat to boots. Claims his coat was once a lord's. It may have been.
fields.ossop_the_unlucky: Human, M. Whatever can go wrong at his stall does: the table tips, the awning leaks, the chicken gets loose. Buyers pity him into sales.
fields.beren_halfcoat: Halfling, M. Lost half his coat (and the story keeps changing about how). Neat, polite, and the most honest haggler in the square.
fields.ivy_scraptongue: Human, F. Sharp-tongued and quick, she trades insults with buyers and wins. Deals mostly in scrap metal and salvage from the capital's workshops.
fields.doras_milkbeard: Human, M. An old man with a long white beard who sells "remedies" of dubious use. Most of them are just tea.
fields.ruel_tinkpocket: Halfling, M. A tinker whose coat is lined with pockets of small broken parts. Fixes cheap trinkets while he haggles.
fields.podge_ashborn: Halfling, M. Round, cheerful and covered in soot, he sells secondhand pots, lanterns and anything that's been near a fire.
fields.uther_nine_debts: Human, M. Owes nine debts to nine people, and keeps careful count. Sells fast and cheap to stay one step ahead of all nine.

- **Ruel Tinkpocket:** Halfling, M. A tinker whose coat is lined with pockets of small broken parts. Fixes cheap trinkets while he haggles.
- **Podge Ashborn:** Halfling, M. Round, cheerful and covered in soot, he sells secondhand pots, lanterns and anything that's been near a fire.
- **Uther Nine-Debts:** Human, M. Owes nine debts to nine people, and keeps careful count. Sells fast and cheap to stay one step ahead of all nine.

entities.body:
The adventurers written onto GuildScribe's parchments. Each one is a character the guild hall (the GuildScribe bot) made for a viewer in a stream's chat, and the name in brackets is the viewer who plays them (left out where the character goes by the viewer's own name).
