entities.name: Chromatic Drake – Xan’s Wildshape
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-07 · Items & inventions._

**Name:** Chromatic Drake – Xan’s Wildshape

**Kind:** Items & Inventions - A temporary transformation utilizing a native race of mana-draining monsters.

**The Rule:** Xan can transform into a shifting, multi-colored drake fueled by stolen mana from other creatures.

**How it Works:** Xan channels ambient mana through his body, stimulating the latent presence of Silvari within him—manifesting them as scales and features before transforming fully. He actively drains mana from nearby animals or people to sustain the form, amplifying its power.

**Costs and Limits:** Requires significant concentration and stamina. Prolonged use risks mental instability in both Xan and anyone nearby. Drakes lasts approximately fifteen minutes before requiring a full recharge (dependent on drained mana). The effectiveness is directly tied to the amount of mana stolen. Only those who possess a naturally high affinity for magic (primarily elves and artificers) are capable of initiating the shift.

**Who it Affects:** Primarily affects any creature within range of Xan's attack/drain; also causes vivid hallucinations. Can disrupt magical workings and potentially damage artifacts sensitive to mana fluctuations. Guards find themselves disoriented when near him.

**What it Changes:** Alters the environment with shimmering distortions, induces hallucinations, and physically shifts the terrain due to displaced elemental energy – briefly creating areas of intense cold or heat. It’s dangerous but powerful.

**Clashes with Canon:** None

**Open Questions:** (suggested) - What is the origin of the Silvari? Are they remnants of another world?

---
In the World: 

The rain hammered against the thick stone walls of Monstradius, mirroring the drumming anxiety beneath Murrow’s workbench. He meticulously adjusted the calibration runes around his Truthglass—a delicate operation designed to authenticate a shipment of gold coming from Stoutwell. Suddenly, a ripple distorted the lens as Xan entered, dripping wet and visibly agitated. “It’s… changing,” he gasped, gesturing wildly towards the shimmering scales forming on his arm. A nearby halfling apprentice stumbled back, clutching his head in confusion, muttering about shifting colors and impossible geometries before collapsing onto the floor. Murrow cursed softly, quickly sealing off the workspace while checking for residual magic–the air felt strangely charged, humming with stolen potential.

entities.name: Marda the Reformed Cutpurse
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-07 · Characters._

Name: Marda the Reformed Cutpurse
Race: Human
Sex: Female
Age: 37 (suggested)
Role: Peddler – specializes in small tools & lockpicks (legally obtained), offering surprisingly sharp advice alongside her wares.
Lives in: Stoutwell - occupies a stall in the central market square.
Appearance: Lean build, perpetually smudged hands, dark eyes that seem to assess everything. Wears practical leather trousers and a worn tunic over a chainmail shirt beneath. Carries several pouches filled with tools and trinkets. A faint scar traces across her left hand.
Personality: Pragmatic, cynical but possesses a dry wit and an unexpected sense of justice. She’s fiercely independent and distrustful of authority figures. Despite her past, she strives to be honest—though sometimes her honesty is delivered with a cutting remark.
Magic: Limited detection magic – primarily used to identify locks and detect subtle alterations or tampering. It's unreliable and drains mana quickly.
Connections: Glumtom (occasional dealings regarding enchanted components); Osric (a wary respect; he occasionally seeks out her expertise for seemingly innocuous tasks). The Elderhold (avoidance; they view her profession with suspicion.)
Secret: Formerly a skilled cutpurse operating within the capital before turning herself in to the Guard. She still retains some of those skills, though rarely uses them overtly.
Story Hooks: 1) A wealthy merchant suspects Marda of being involved in a recent theft targeting his valuables. 2) An artifact stolen from the capital arrives in Stoutwell, and its thief is believed to have connections to Marda. 3) Osric needs her assistance decoding a complex mechanism found during a dig site – one that may hold dangerous secrets.

Who they are: Marda is a survivor, forged by hardship and regret. Her former life as a thief instilled in her a keen eye for detail, a knack for unlocking things (both literal and figurative), and a deep-seated distrust of power. Now, she runs a modest stall offering tools and advice, attempting to use her unique skillset for honest gain while perpetually looking over her shoulder. Her past haunts her, fueling both her cynicism and her desire to atone—though whether she truly believes she’s earned redemption remains an open question.

entities.name: Northwind Harbour & Surrounding Mountains
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Regions & places._

**Name:** Northwind Harbour & Surrounding Mountains

**Kind:** Regions & Places – Mountainous coastal region north of Arandur’s capital.

**The Rule:** Travel through the mountainous area surrounding Northwind Harbour requires specialized knowledge and carries inherent risks due to unpredictable terrain and dangerous creatures.

**How It Works:** Travelers utilize experienced guides familiar with mountain paths, employing featherhooks for assisted climbing and relying on detection magic to anticipate creature movements and potential hazards - skilled navigators are rare and expensive.

**Costs and Limits:** Navigation costs include guide fees (1-3 silver pieces per day), supplies (rations, rope, healing potions—5-10 silver pieces per week), and potentially weapon repairs/replacement if damaged by stonekin or wyverns. Limited by poor visibility, treacherous terrain, and constant threat of predation.  A strong wind can make travel near impossible.

**Who It Affects:** Primarily travelers, merchants, soldiers, and the settlement of Stonehaven itself relies on timber and resources from these mountains. The Stonekin actively resist intrusion.

**What It Changes:** Introduces new trade routes, expands the Kingdom's territory (albeit tenuously controlled), creates opportunities for encounters with unusual monsters, and adds a layer of danger to any journey outside the established roads. 

**Clashes With Canon:** None

**Open Questions:** (Suggested) – What is the nature of the Stonekin’s resistance? How do the wyvern populations relate to other known monstrous threats in Verrowen?

In the world, Master Tobin Ashby stood at the edge of the Scarred Pass, his face weathered by wind and sun. His apprentice, young Elias, nervously adjusted the featherhook strapped to his wrist as they prepared to descend into the ravine. A thick fog clung to the mountain slopes, muting sound and obscuring vision - a familiar hazard intensified by the presence of the elusive Stonekin, whose low growls echoed faintly through the rock. He consulted Murrow’s Lodestone, its mirrorstone surface swirling with faint patterns indicating movement within the stone; it was time to proceed carefully, lest they trigger an ancient conflict.

entities.name: Greyhaven
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Regions & places._

**Name:** Greyhaven

**Kind:** Regions & Places - A district within Stoutwell, bordering the Ashen Reach and the Guard Training Grounds.

**The Rule:** Greyhaven is defined by its proximity to the training grounds and the constant flow of ash dust from the Ashen Reach, creating a perpetually gritty environment inhabited primarily by those unable to afford better housing.

**How It Works:**  The district’s economy relies on scavenging, repair work, and informal trade facilitated by Doric's smithy, benefiting directly from discarded materials and surplus equipment from the Guard's training exercises.

**Costs and Limits:** Accessing Greyhaven requires navigating dangerous conditions – ash inhalation causing chronic illness, frequent flooding, and potential encounters with wild beasts drawn to the exposed area. Mana expenditure is minimal here, mostly related to simple repairs or warding against minor environmental hazards. 

**Who It Affects:** Primarily impoverished human families, some halflings, former Guard recruits, and occasional itinerant laborers seeking temporary employment. The Elderhold maintains nominal oversight but exerts little direct control. 

**What It Changes:** Greyhaven subtly shifts Stoutwell’s social dynamic, acting as a visible reminder of inequality and providing a steady stream of low-skilled labor for the kingdom (and occasionally, unfortunately, for criminal enterprises). 

**Clashes With Canon:** None. 

**Open Questions:** (Suggested) - *What specific illnesses are prevalent in Greyhaven due to the ash?*

---
In the world:

Rain hammered down on the corrugated iron roof of Silas’s workshop, drumming out a relentless rhythm alongside the clang of his hammer. He was painstakingly repairing a shattered shield for Corporal Garin, one of the newest Guardsmen emerging from the drills below. A fine layer of grey dust coated everything—Silas’s hands, his tools, even the meager meal he'd eaten before starting.  The smell of burnt timber mingled with the damp earth; the familiar scent of Greyhaven – a grim testament to Stoutwell’s edges. Murrow would soon be by, demanding an inventory report for Doric’s materials.

**The Rule:** Greyhaven is defined by its proximity to the training grounds and the constant flow of ash dust from the Ashen Reach, creating a perpetually gritty environment inhabited primarily by those unable to afford better housing.

**How It Works:**  The district’s economy relies on scavenging, repair work, and informal trade facilitated by Doric's smithy, benefiting directly from discarded materials and surplus equipment from the Guard's training exercises.

**Costs and Limits:** Accessing Greyhaven requires navigating dangerous conditions – ash inhalation causing chronic illness, frequent flooding, and potential encounters with wild beasts drawn to the exposed area. Mana expenditure is minimal here, mostly related to simple repairs or warding against minor environmental hazards. 

**Who It Affects:** Primarily impoverished human families, some halflings, former Guard recruits, and occasional itinerant laborers seeking temporary employment. The Elderhold maintains nominal oversight but exerts little direct control. 

**What It Changes:** Greyhaven subtly shifts Stoutwell’s social dynamic, acting as a visible reminder of inequality and providing a steady stream of low-skilled labor for the kingdom (and occasionally, unfortunately, for criminal enterprises). 

**Clashes With Canon:** None. 

**Open Questions:** (Suggested) - *What specific illnesses are prevalent in Greyhaven due to the ash?*

entities.name: Saltwind Reach
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Regions & places._

Name: Saltwind Reach

Kind (Regions & Places): The Reach is notoriously difficult to navigate, prone to sudden squalls and monstrous marine life, demanding experienced sailors and sturdy vessels; attempting landings during poor weather can prove fatal.

How it Works: Remnants of fortified coastal settlements dot the shoreline – evidence of earlier, smaller kingdoms that fell to the tides centuries ago. These were built not as grand fortresses but rather as practical tidal defenses against raiding parties from across the Narrow Sea. Local shipwrights utilize techniques passed down through generations, specializing in building ‘stormbreakers’ - ships reinforced with ironwood salvaged from shipwrecks. The reach's unique currents and seabed formations attract unusual fish populations – giant crabs and bioluminescent eels are common catches.

Costs and Limits: Passage costs 1 Mana per day (primarily for navigating treacherous currents). A successful landing attempt requires at least two seasoned sailors (1 Mana/day each) and a set of 'sea hooks' crafted by local shipwrights (6 silver coins per hook), which often require regular maintenance. Injury within the reach incurs a 2 Mana cost—often worsened by cuts and bruises aggravated by jagged rocks. Severe weather necessitates reinforced stormbreakers and skilled captains – adding significantly to travel time.

Who it Affects: Primarily fishermen, traders passing through, occasional royal surveyors, and the handful of hardy souls who call Saltwind Reach home. Stoutwell relies on its catch, though trade is limited due to the hazards.

What it Changes: Its remote location limits sustained trade or significant Royal influence; represents a valuable source of rare materials and potential escape routes for dissidents.

Clashes with canon (or “None”): None

Open questions: (suggested) What specific creatures inhabit the deeper coves near the ruins?

In the world:
The rain hammered against the timbers of Silas’s small fishing boat as he hauled in his evening catch - mostly sea-slugs and phosphorescent shrimp. The wind howled off the cliffs, carrying spray that stung his face. Old Man Hemlock, mending nets beside him, grunted, "Stormbreaker's holding true tonight, boy. Best build in Verrowen hasn't seen conditions like this in a generation." A flash of blue light briefly illuminated from beneath the waves before disappearing into the dark depths--a common sight around Saltwind Reach, but always unsettling enough to make Silas check his hooks twice.

entities.name: Gilded Spine of the Silent Archivist
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Anything._

Name: Gilded Spine of the Silent Archivist
Kind: Object - Relic
What it is: This intricate silver locket whispers fragments of betrayal whenever worn by someone who has betrayed another person, amplifying their guilt and suspicion.
The Details: The Spine manifests as fleeting auditory hallucinations—not full conversations, but snippets of phrases laced with accusation (“You lied…”, “I knew…”). The volume increases proportionally to the wearer’s stress levels or proximity to individuals they distrust. Osric would experience fragmented thoughts concerning his role within the Elderhold, subtly questioning loyalties amongst his peers – he wouldn't be driven mad, but certainly frustrated and paranoid. Silas initially experiences vague unease before being drawn towards more defined whispers related to those around him. The whispers don't *reveal* concrete betrayals, just the potential for them, feeding a cycle of paranoia and investigation. Murrow hypothesizes that the item draws on ambient magical echoes of past transgressions – lingering ‘residue’ from significant lies and broken oaths.

Clashes with canon (None)
Open questions: (Suggested) Trigger mechanism specifics (how does it activate?), Precise effect range/intensity (how loud are the whispers?) , Source of the magic (where did this relic come from?). 

In the world:

Silas clutched the Gilded Spine tightly, the cool metal strangely comforting against his burning brow. He was sitting in the Wellhouse tavern, nursing a pint of Stoutwell ale - an attempt at calming the incessant murmurings within his mind. A snippet of voice drifted through the room - "He promised me safety...but left me exposed." It wasn’t directed at anyone specific; rather a generalized echo of broken trust swirling within his skull.  The other patrons barely noticed his frown, engrossed in their own conversations, oblivious to the spectral accusations warring beneath his awareness. He took another gulp of ale, hoping to drown out the voices, but they persisted, unsettling reminders of his fractured past and the unknown dangers ahead.

entities.name: Reinforced Gatehouse Beams
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Items & inventions._

**Name:** Reinforced Gatehouse Beams

**Kind (Items & Inventions):** Structural Enhancement via Elemental Infusion

**The Rule:** Iron-banded oak beams reinforced with controlled elemental fire increase the structural integrity of the Stoutwell gatehouse against siege weaponry.

**How it Works:** Doric forges oak beams with bands of iron, while Murrow subtly infuses them with channeled elemental fire – strengthening the wood’s grain through heat manipulation, layering a weak ward against impact. 

**Costs and Limits:** Approximately 8-9 silver pieces per beam, labor from slum workers supplementing Doric's work (estimated 2 copper per day), risk of instability if Murrow overloads the infusion—potentially causing damage or injury (risk factor: medium). Primarily affects the guard rotation and those working near the gate. It strengthens the gatehouse considerably but doesn’t dramatically alter its appearance.

**Who it Affects:** Doric (primary artisan), Murrow (manipulator of the magic), Guard Rotation (users of the strengthened structure), Slum Workers (labor force), potentially all residents within range of potential instabilities.

**What it Changes:** Increases the gatehouse’s resistance to projectile attacks and blunt force trauma; shifts focus towards needing maintenance/monitoring by someone skilled in detecting magical disturbances. 

**Clashes with Canon:** None

**Open Questions:** (Suggested) - *“Does this significantly reduce the chance of a rift opening directly at the gate?”*

In the world, the afternoon sun cast long shadows across the newly reinforced section of the Stoutwell Gatehouse as Tobin Ashby hammered a final rivet into place. The air still carried a faint scent of smoke – a subtle reminder of Murrow's careful work. A couple of grizzled guardsmen shifted uneasily, checking their shields, while Murrow adjusted his spectacles, meticulously examining the grain pattern of the oak for any signs of distress. The rhythmic clang of metal against metal mingled with the shouts of the slum workers hauling timber nearby, creating an oddly ordered scene amidst the rough-hewn village, solidifying the fortified frontier against the looming Monster Wood.

_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Characters._

**Xan**

Race: Dragonborn
Sex: Male
Age: Approximately 58 (appears younger due to lessened magic)
Role: Wandering Peddler / Occasional Observer (Burn's 'regular')
Lives in: The capital city – specifically, the sprawling marketplace known as “The Hub” – though he has a small workshop near the GuildScribe Hall.
Appearance: Lean build, scaled dark grey-blue like polished obsidian, unusually short horns that curve backwards sharply over his brow. Wears a mismatched collection of travel clothes - mostly patched leather and faded silks - layered beneath a worn brown cloak. Always carries the Pot of Greed prominently displayed within a simple cloth pouch at his belt. He favors spectacles perched on his nose (badly made).
Personality: Dry wit, cynical observation, unnervingly calm even under pressure. Possesses an unsettling habit of staring intently without blinking, often accompanied by a subtle smirk. A master of understated sarcasm and enjoys nothing more than observing human folly.  (Suggested - He possesses a deep, almost painful melancholy masked by his sharp tongue.)
Magic: Limited elemental manipulation—primarily focused on minor illusions and creating fleeting visual distractions. His skill is low; only capable of producing brief flashes of light or shimmering mirages. When using it, he gets noticeably colder.
Connections: The Wellhouse elves (a reluctant acquaintance), Murrow (his creator/occasional supplier), Hesketh Reeve (Captain of the Guard) – with whom he maintains a strained truce via Burn’s observations. The Scribe (through gossip about the GuildScribe's adventurers), Glumtom (the Reanimator in the capital)
Secret: Knows the location of one of the hidden passages leading from the mountain wall into Verrowen—though he refuses to reveal its purpose or destination. 
Story Hooks: Rumors persist that Xan was once part of a royal expedition sent to investigate strange rifts opening across the kingdom. He claims to have “seen things” he can barely articulate. He’s been seen discreetly collecting information regarding the Elderhold’s activities.

**Who they are:** Xan is an enigma wrapped in cynicism and a ludicrously useless trinket. He drifts through the bustling marketplace of the capital like a shadow, observing everyone with unsettling intensity. Having spent decades chasing shadows and rumors, his true motivations remain deliberately obscure, obscured by layers of carefully constructed irony. Despite his sardonic demeanor, there’s a palpable sadness beneath the surface - a lingering echo of something lost or perhaps never fully possessed. It's this quiet melancholy which makes him such a strangely compelling fixture in Stoutwell’s world – and particularly within Burn’s orbit.

entities.name: Mana Affinity Items
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Magic._

**Name:** Mana Affinity Items

**Kind (Magic):** Personal Magic Reserves – Specialized items react differently based on the wielder’s inherent magical capacity and training.

**The Rule:** “Magic usage isn’t uniform across all individuals; inherent aptitude—particularly demonstrated early through Murrow’s Elemental Test—dictates a baseline mana reserve, amplified significantly when focusing on a specific magical discipline.”

**How it Works:**  Items respond most effectively to those whose innate affinity aligns with their function, minimizing mana expenditure and maximizing output. A mismatch leads to inefficiency, increased drain, and potential instability.

**Costs & Limits:** Item creation costs vary dramatically depending on materials *and* required mana stabilization - approximately 10 silver coins + 2 Mana for basic enchanted iron shield. Advanced items require exponentially higher investment. Constant use drains reserves faster; overuse can cause fatigue or collapse.

**Who It Affects:** Primarily skilled artisans, traders, and combatants utilizing specialized magic-infused tools and equipment. The Guard relies heavily upon Hesketh's enhanced strength. Those lacking training will experience significant drawbacks.

**What It Changes:** Creates stratification within Verrowen society – favouring naturally gifted individuals who control powerful magical objects, potentially widening gaps between wealth/status and creating new avenues of influence.

**Clashes With Canon:** None

**Open Questions:** (Suggested) How does this affect the efficiency of artificer created works vs. natural ones?

---
In the world:

The rain hammered against the canvas roof of Doric’s smithy as he painstakingly forged a new haft for an arrow. Young Tobin, sweat dripping from his brow, struggled to maintain focus, his face flushed with exertion. Doric, with a subtle gesture, channeled a trickle of calming energy—a faint blue shimmer—into the metal, smoothing out imperfections and bolstering its resilience. He was instinctively using his inherent affinity for heat and shaping, reducing the need for brute force and minimizing the drain on *his* mana. Even Tobin, despite his youthful enthusiasm, felt the familiar tingle of depletion after only a few minutes; a stark reminder that true mastery demanded more than just muscle and ambition.

**Kind (Magic):** Personal Magic Reserves – Specialized items react differently based on the wielder’s inherent magical capacity and training.

**The Rule:** “Magic usage isn't uniform across all individuals; inherent aptitude—particularly demonstrated early through Murrow’s Elemental Test—dictates a baseline mana reserve, amplified significantly when focusing on a specific magical discipline.”

**How it Works:** Items actively channeling magic experience accelerated degradation rates proportional to the type of mana being utilized. Elemental types degrade fastest, followed by strength enhancement, while detection spells cause rapid destabilization.

**Costs & Limits:** Item creation costs vary dramatically depending on materials *and* required mana stabilization - approximately 10 silver coins + 2 Mana for basic enchanted iron shield. Each item possesses a ‘Stability Rating,’ tracked through minor repairs using specialized oils and finely-cut gemstones. Excessive use or poorly managed application chips away at this rating. Failure results in complete loss of function, requiring full reconstruction.

**Who It Affects:** Primarily skilled artisans, traders, and combatants utilizing specialized magic-infused tools and equipment. The Guard relies heavily upon Hesketh’s enhanced strength. Those lacking training will experience significant drawbacks.

**What It Changes:** Creates stratification within Verrowen society – favouring naturally gifted individuals who control powerful magical objects, potentially widening gaps between wealth/status and creating new avenues of influence.

**Clashes with canon (or “None”):** None

**Open questions:** (Suggested) How does this affect the efficiency of artificer created works vs. natural ones?

In the world: Doric meticulously sharpened an arrowhead against his whetstone, sweat stinging his eyes. He'd just finished reinforcing the Featherhook attachment—a shimmering blue energy momentarily etching itself into the iron. A tiny plume of grey smoke escaped as he applied stabilizing oil, its scent sharp and metallic. Tobin watched him, fidgeting impatiently, acutely aware that pushing the Featherhook too hard would likely cause immediate failure - he knew better than to ask about it. The air around Doric thrummed faintly with heat, a visual echo of the immense effort channeled through the tool; a subtle reminder of the price demanded for mastery.

entities.name: Resonance Stone Device
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Items & inventions._

**Name:** Resonance Stone Device

**Kind:** Items & Inventions – A handheld device utilizing a resonance stone to passively amplify ambient magical signatures.

**The Rule:** This device allows a single operator to detect nearby magic through enhanced sensory input, providing rudimentary awareness of their surroundings.

**How it Works:** A finely-tuned resonator chamber within the device captures and amplifies subtle magical emanations, translating them into tactile sensations - warmth, pressure, slight vibrations – relayed directly to the operator’s nervous system via fine copper wiring connected to gloves. 

**Costs and Limits:** Three weeks of skilled smithing labor (Doric's work), approximately 25 silver coins for components, three days extracting a resonance stone from the Monster Wood, limited range dependent on surrounding mana strength, drains stone quickly with prolonged use, susceptible to feedback loops at overuse. 

**Who it Affects:** Primarily intended for individuals sensitive to magic—likely those untrained or inexperienced in detection—potentially useful for guards, scouts, and investigators needing basic situational awareness. It could also be used by Murrow himself for reconnaissance.

**What it Changes:** Shifts perception; transforms passive observation into active sensing. Doesn't grant true "detection" but augments existing sensitivity, making users more attuned to fluctuations in magical energy.

**Clashes with Canon:** None.

**Open Questions:** (Suggested) The specific type of ‘sensations’ experienced will vary greatly depending on ambient magic; is there a way to standardize this? How does Glumtom’s Reanimator technology interact with such amplified signatures?

In the world:

The rain hammered against the slate roof of Monstradius as Murrow adjusted the Resonance Stone Device, its grey surface gleaming faintly beneath the workshop’s single oil lamp. A young Guard recruit, Tobin Ashby, stood awkwardly beside him, clad in leather gloves connected to the device.  Tobin shifted nervously, his face etched with concentration – a faint flush warming his cheeks as he described the subtle vibrations - “Like a swarm of tiny bees buzzing…almost.” Murrow nodded gravely, meticulously adjusting a copper coil. This wasn't grand detection magic, just a carefully calibrated link between human senses and the chaotic whispers of Verrowen's inherent magic, a start toward understanding something far greater.

Name: Rootwraiths
Kind: Plant/Spirit (Entanglement)
The Rule: These animated root constructs attempt to ensnare creatures within their grasping tendrils.
How It Works: They move slowly, relying on surprise attacks and attempting to grapple targets using thorny vines. Success requires a successful Dexterity saving throw against their reach and bludgeoning damage.
Costs and Limits: Vulnerable to fire damage, requiring significant effort to destroy.  Detection requires a high Perception roll.
Who It Affects: Primarily melee fighters, archers struggling to maintain aim under pressure.
What It Changes: Introduces a constant threat of being restrained and slowed down by spectral vegetation.
Clashes With Canon: None
Open Questions: (Suggested) – Can they be reasoned with or manipulated?

---

Name: Gloomshrooms
Kind: Fungus/Psychic (Hallucination)
The Rule: These clusters release spores that induce vivid nightmares and disorientation in those nearby.
How It Works: The spores require a DC12 Wisdom save to resist; failure results in temporary madness - confusion, paranoia, and reduced actions for one round. Bright light rapidly disperses the spores.
Costs and Limits: Requires proximity to avoid. Vulnerability to bright light. Limited range. 
Who It Affects: Individuals susceptible to fear or anxiety are more vulnerable. Those with low wisdom scores take a higher penalty. 
What It Changes: Alters perception, reduces combat effectiveness, creates opportunities for manipulation.
Clashes With Canon: None
Open Questions: (suggested) – How long do effects last? Do certain herbs provide resistance? 

---

Name: Stonegrubs
Kind: Earth/Animal (Burrowing Assault)
The Rule: These armored grubs use their burrowing abilities to ambush targets from beneath the ground.
How it works: They move quickly through loose earth and stone, attempting to grapple prey with powerful jaws. Attacks involve Dexterity saving throws against piercing damage and potentially stunning targets.
Costs & Limits: Slow movement on hard surfaces. Effectiveness depends heavily on terrain – requires soft soil.  Vulnerable to blunt attacks. 
Who It Affects: Primarily melee fighters caught off-guard, those moving through wooded areas.
What It Changes: Introduces an element of surprise and vulnerability during travel or battle.
Clashes With Canon: None
Open Questions: (Suggested) - Can they be lured into traps? 

---

Name: Shadowhawks
Kind: Animal/Darkness (Silent Predation)
The Rule: These evolved hawks utilize darkness and silent flight to harass and incapacitate prey. 
How It Works: Benefit from low light conditions; have advantage on stealth checks in shadows. Their attack relies on a single hit, but follow up attacks can easily overwhelm a target with overwhelming speed. 
Costs & Limits: Vulnerable to bright light and fire. Requires careful tracking and positioning. 
Who It Affects: Archers, scouts, any vulnerable creature exposed without cover. 
What It Changes: Adds a new aerial threat to the Deep Woods. 
Clashes With Canon: None
Open Questions: (suggested) – Do they leave behind traces after their strikes? 

**In the World:**

The morning mist clung to Stoutwell’s croplands as Silas, the village woodcutter, strained against the weight of a fallen branch. He paused

entities.name: The Emerald Echoes - A revitalized gem of Verrowen’s history
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-09 · Peoples & groups._

Okay, here we go – let’ a little bit more polish on the idea!

**Name:** The Emerald Echoes - A revitalized gem of Verrowen’s history.

**Kind:** Ancient relics and legends, intimately tied to the Kingdom’s prosperity.

**The Rule:** History is meticulously preserved and interpreted through skilled GuildScribes, ensuring the truth resonates throughout all regions.

**How it Works:**  Historians use subtle techniques—a glance at an artifact, a whispered question—to establish narratives that reflect how people actually lived. This ensures consistency across the realm's records.

**Costs and Limits:** Relatively low; primarily reliant on the integrity of archives and the expertise of the guild. Minor adjustments are easy; a few whispers of revision.

**Who it Affects:** Everyone living in Verrowen – citizens, merchants, even travelers seeking a glimpse into its past. But most specifically: Historian'*s Guild members (and anyone who appreciates a good story).

**What it Changes:** Stories about the kingdom's founding, landmarks, heroes and more being actively revived & improved. Old stories get re-written with fresh details -- like the tale of the Golden Lantern's origin. It boosts tourism as well.

**Clashes with Canon:** None - established interpretations exist but always ripe for refinement. Is there an established “official” view of King Silas’ first day? 

**In the world:** The sun shines warm over the cobbled streets of Stoutwell, cobblestones gleaming under the gentle light of morning. A small crowd has gathered outside the Wellhouse tavern, eager to hear tales from their beloved GuildScribe, Esmeralda Willowbrook. The air is thick with anticipation, fueled by freshly baked pastries and the promise of a vibrant history lesson.

entities.name: Orin Bellweather
entities.filed_from: From a lore-keeper chat
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-10 · Characters._

**Name:** Orin Bellweather
**Race:** Human
**Sex:** Male
**Age:** Approximately 67 years (appears younger due to consistent routine & minimal magic exposure)
**Role:** Town Crier – Stoutwell (Guild Contractor)
**Lives in:** GuildScribe Hall, Capital City – Primary office within the main hall.
**Appearance:** Lean build, approximately six feet tall, dressed in a meticulously maintained crimson tunic embroidered with silver heraldic motifs - depicting a stylized bell intertwined with wheat stalks. He wears polished leather boots and carries a large, intricately carved wooden staff topped with a resonant bronze bell. His grey hair is neatly combed back, revealing a weathered face marked by good humour and countless announcements.
**Personality:** Cheerful, punctual, theatrical, and dependable. Orin treats every announcement as important, even when the news is only that an ad break has been delayed. He speaks like a professional herald but has picked up the relaxed humor of tavern life. He is never cruel or intrusive, prefers clear facts to speculation, and dislikes being ignored. Orin is patient with newcomers, mildly dramatic when a schedule changes, and secretly proud that he can keep an entire room of adventurers informed without interrupting the story. (suggested)
**Magic:** Limited elemental influence – primarily focused on amplifying his voice for greater projection and subtly adjusting ambient sounds within the hall to ensure optimal clarity. It's largely ceremonial rather than practical.
**Connections:** Serves under Master Silas Thorne (GuildScribe). Maintains informal contact with merchants throughout Stoutwell & surrounding settlements. Operates alongside Thomas Penwright (Stoutwell Town Crier), sharing information regarding local events and potential disruptions. (suggested)
**Secret:** Possesses a minor talent for manipulating echoes – capable of creating brief sonic illusions to add emphasis or create diversions during particularly urgent broadcasts. This ability stems from a childhood spent exploring abandoned catacombs beneath the GuildScribe Hall. 
**Story Hooks:** Knowledgeable about the Kingdom’s political landscape and historical events; potentially holds key information relating to the founding of Stoutwell or forgotten royal decrees. His frequent travels could lead him into conflict with criminal organizations seeking to exploit his position. Has been observed discreetly communicating with Murrow, possibly investigating unusual magical activity in Stoutwell.

entities.name: Willa Stonebridge
entities.filed_from: From a Claude session
entities.body:
_From a Claude session, 2026-11-10 · Characters._

**Name:** Willa Stonebridge
**Race:** Halfling
**Sex:** Female
**Age:** 74
**Role:** Senior shield-bearer of the Guard – Stoutwell
**Lives in:** Stoutwell, in a cottage by the wall, close enough to hear the wardbell.
**Appearance:** Broad even for a stout halfling, with forearms like a smith's and grey hair cut short for under a helmet. She fights from behind a Guard shield almost as tall as she is, and when she plants it — Standfast — she looks less like a soldier than like part of the wall that got up and moved.
**Personality:** Patient, dry, and immovable in every sense. She has trained half the village's rotation shield-bearers and corrects a stance the way other people comment on the weather. She thinks panic is just fear that hasn't been given a job yet.
**Magic:** None of her own to speak of. Her shield carries the magic for her.
**Connections:** Captain Hesketh Reeve leans on her for the wall and cropland rotations. Doric forged her shield. Fenwick Larkspur was already a retired Elder when she joined, and she still brings him the Guard's news first, out of old respect.
**Secret:** Standfast is unmarked Monstradius work. Murrow set its stone years ago, before she understood what an unmarked enchantment could make people ask, and she has never told the Elderhold who did it.
**Story Hooks:** The shield Guard is small and overworked, and Willa is its oldest full-timer: if she falls, no one is ready to hold the middle of the line. And if the Kingdom ever asks questions about unmarked Guard gear, her, Murrow and the Elderhold are in a bind at once.

fields.what_it_is: An enchanted Guard shield — one of the big shields Stoutwell's halfling shield-bearers fight from behind, almost fully hidden. Doric forged it; its boss is set with a charged stone.
fields.who: Carried by Willa Stonebridge, the Guard's senior shield-bearer.
fields.where: Stoutwell — the walls, the croplands, and wherever the shield line forms.
fields.how_it_works: While its bearer braces with the shield planted, the stone drinks the force of blows: pushes, charges and rootwyrm lunges that should bowl a halfling over leave her standing. When the stored force passes what the stone can hold, the shield sheds it as a single deep bell-note — the line's warning that its anchor is at her limit.
fields.limits: The charge fades like any enchanted item's, and recharging means Monstradius. Bracing roots the bearer too: planted, she cannot dodge, turn quickly or retreat until she lifts the shield. And the stone holds force, not edges — a blade that gets around the shield hurts her like anyone.
fields.ties: It carries no artificer's mark, because Murrow set the stone. Kingdom-made Guard gear is supposed to be marked, and everyone in Stoutwell knows what unmarked work makes people ask.

_From a Claude session, 2026-11-10 · Characters._

**Name:** Corin Hale
**Race:** Human
**Sex:** Male
**Age:** 35
**Role:** Sergeant of the Guard – Stoutwell; Hesketh Reeve's second
**Lives in:** Stoutwell, in the guardhouse rooms by the gate.
**Appearance:** Tall, lean, and scarred along the left forearm where a shield rim caught him as a recruit. He wears Lamplight at his hip even off duty, and drills the rotation villagers in the yard behind the guardhouse — patient with the clumsy, merciless with the lazy.
**Personality:** Steady, fair in his captain's mold, and funnier than he looks; his drill-yard insults are a village institution. He believes the rotation works because ordinary people rise to being trusted with a wall.
**Magic:** A trace, like most humans: he can coax a wick or a campfire alight. He lets people assume Lamplight's glow is his doing and corrects no one.
**Connections:** Hesketh Reeve's right hand and likely successor. Willa Stonebridge's shield-bearers are what his sword-and-bill drills are built around. Tobin Ashby served his own rotation days under Corin.
**Secret:** He can barely read. Duty rosters and tithe tallies are read to him by whoever is on clerk duty, and he memorizes them whole. Bertram Quillby may suspect — and the Elder's skimmed ledgers would be much safer if the Guard's sergeant never learns to check them himself.
**Story Hooks:** If Hesketh falls or is called away, the Guard is Corin's, illiteracy and all. And a sergeant who memorizes every roster he has ever been read is a walking record of who dodged which shifts — leverage several people would rather he didn't have.

fields.what_it_is: An enchanted short sword — a sergeant's sidearm rather than a hero's blade. Its hilt is ash wood from the Ashen Reach, the wood Stoutwell's woodworkers prize for weapon hilts.
fields.who: Carried by Corin Hale, sergeant of Stoutwell's Guard, and by the sergeants before him.
fields.where: Made in the Kingdom and come down through the Guard from sergeant to sergeant; carried now on Stoutwell's walls and night rotation.
fields.how_it_works: Drawn after dark, the blade sheds a soft candle-glow — enough to read a roster by, check a latch, or see the step in front of you on the wall, and not enough to blind its bearer. Its edge also simply refuses to dull: seasons of use have never once needed a whetstone.
fields.limits: The glow is small and honest — it lights a page, not a battlefield, and it tells anything watching from the dark exactly where the sergeant stands. The enchantment fades like any other; on the night it runs out mid-watch, Lamplight is just a well-kept sword.
fields.ties: It carries a registered Kingdom artificer's mark on the ricasso, worn nearly smooth with age — the opposite of Monstradius work, and a quiet reminder that the Guard's gear wasn't always village-made.

entities.name: Sella Vane
entities.filed_from: From a Claude session
entities.body:
_From a Claude session, 2026-11-10 · Characters._

**Name:** Sella Vane
**Race:** Human
**Sex:** Female
**Age:** 41
**Role:** Escort to a regular merchant of the Woodland Road
**Lives in:** Mostly the road. Stoutwell, the lake settlement and the capital are her three addresses, and she pays rent at none of them.
**Appearance:** Weathered, close-cropped hair gone grey early, a throwing axe — Comeback — at her belt and a second, ordinary axe for firewood and emphasis. She walks a pace behind the cart and to its left, always, and scans clearings the way other people check the weather.
**Personality:** Easy company and hard to surprise. She tells road stories freely — other people's. Merchants trust her because goods under her eye simply stop going missing.
**Magic:** None. She is openly suspicious of enchanted gear she has to rely on, Comeback being the single exception, which she argues with like an old friend.
**Connections:** Hired season after season by the same merchant, who runs goods between Stoutwell, the lake settlement and the capital road. Known by sight to the Guard's gathering escorts, and a familiar face to the road peddlers.
**Secret:** In her twenties she was the thing escorts guard against: a robber on the Woodland Road, never caught and never named. She knows where the ambushes are because she picked half the spots herself. Her merchant knows. It is exactly why he hires her.
**Story Hooks:** If robbery rises on the road again, Sella will recognize the work — either because it's hers, copied, or because an old partner is back. And her past is the one thing that could end her livelihood if the wrong Elder or the wrong tax man hears it.

fields.what_it_is: An enchanted throwing axe, balanced for the hand and the air alike.
fields.who: Carried by Sella Vane, a merchant's escort on the Woodland Road.
fields.where: The Woodland Road and the capital road. Made somewhere along them — Sella names a different town every time anyone asks.
fields.how_it_works: Thrown, and called with a sharp whistle in the one note Sella taught it, it pulls out of wood, ground or worse and flies back to her hand. On a cart, in a ditch, mid-ambush, she is never unarmed for long.
fields.limits: Each return drinks its stored mana; a drained Comeback is a good axe that stays where it lands until it is recharged. It returns only to the hand that threw it — no one else's whistle works — and it cannot pull free of a closed door, a strong grip, or deep water.
fields.ties: An escort's weapon through and through: useless for holding a wall, perfect for a road where trouble comes out of the treeline and goes back to it.

entities.name: Vesper Harrowmere
entities.filed_from: From a Claude session
entities.body:
_From a Claude session, 2026-11-10 · Characters._

**Name:** Vesper Harrowmere
**Race:** Elf
**Sex:** Female
**Age:** 212
**Role:** Champion of House Harrowmere, holder of the Highwrit – the capital
**Lives in:** The capital, in House Harrowmere's rooms by the Rolls House.
**Appearance:** Tall and still in the elven way, dark hair dressed with a clerk's plainness that fools no one, and Quill at her hip in a sheath tooled like a scroll case. At court she dresses like paperwork and moves like a thrown knife.
**Personality:** Precise, courteous, and dry to the point of cruelty. She treats a duel as an edit: something badly written is struck out, once, neatly. Two centuries of court have left her bored by everything except a genuinely good argument or a genuinely good fencer.
**Magic:** More than most — elves stand first in the world's magic — but she spends hers on small perfections: a page that never smudges, a blade oiled by a look. In a duel she uses none at all, by house rule and personal pride.
**Connections:** Kin to the head of House Harrowmere, whose Highwrit her duels defend: challenges to the house's documents, seals and honor land on her point. She knows GuildScribe's hall, and its Scribe, by reputation and old business.
**Secret:** She has never killed anyone. Every duel of her career has ended at the signature — Quill's hair-thin silver scar — and the court's belief that she is lethal rests entirely on her never saying otherwise.
**Story Hooks:** A duel she cannot end at first blood — a challenger who refuses the signature and fights on — would crack a legend the whole capital leans on. And a house whose honor is one woman's two-hundred-year bluff is a house one bad evening from scandal.

entities.name: Pell Ashdown
entities.filed_from: From a Claude session
entities.body:
_From a Claude session, 2026-11-10 · Characters._

**Name:** Pell Ashdown
**Race:** Halfling
**Sex:** Male
**Age:** 52
**Role:** Lead hand and fighter of the dead-tree runs – Stoutwell
**Lives in:** Stoutwell, at the village edge nearest the Monster Wood, because the runs start before dawn and he likes the walk short.
**Appearance:** Wiry rather than stout, weathered dark by outdoor years, with a felling axe — Rootbane — that has been re-hafted so many times the head is the only original part anyone can prove. He smells faintly of sap and woodsmoke most days.
**Personality:** Cheerful, unhurried, and quietly brave in the specific way of people who work where the monsters are. He judges people by how they behave in the wood: who goes quiet, who watches the treeline, and who jokes to cover fear — he counts the third kind the most dangerous and the most useful.
**Magic:** A woodman's trace of it: splinters ease out of his hands on their own, and he always knows which way the village is. Whether that is magic or fifty years of woodcraft, Pell declines to settle.
**Connections:** The dead-tree runs are the Guard escorts' other duty, and he works alongside their archers and shield-bearers; Willa Stonebridge trusts his read of the wood over any scout's report. Doric re-hafts and re-edges Rootbane, and pretends not to notice the enchantment when he does.
**Secret:** Years ago, following a sound like the wood holding its breath, he found a place in the Monster Wood where the air goes thin, the way it does at a rift's edge — and said nothing. He marked it with a cairn of stacked stones only he would recognize, checks the cairn on every run, and has never once decided what to do if it changes.
**Story Hooks:** The Blight does not stand still, and Pell's cairn is the village's only unwritten early warning of it moving. If the thin place widens, the woodcutter who never reported it becomes the most important person in Stoutwell.

entities.where: Stoutwell, at the village edge nearest the Monster Wood, because the runs start before dawn and he likes the walk short.
entities.magic: A woodman's trace of it: splinters ease out of his hands on their own, and he always knows which way the village is. Whether that is magic or fifty years of woodcraft, Pell declines to settle.
entities.personality: Cheerful, unhurried, and quietly brave in the specific way of people who work where the monsters are. He judges people by how they behave in the wood: who goes quiet, who watches the treeline, and who jokes to cover fear — he counts the third kind the most dangerous and the most useful.
entities.appearance: Wiry rather than stout, weathered dark by outdoor years, with a felling axe — Rootbane — that has been re-hafted so many times the head is the only original part anyone can prove. He smells faintly of sap and woodsmoke most days.
entities.secret: Years ago, following a sound like the wood holding its breath, he found a place in the Monster Wood where the air goes thin, the way it does at a rift's edge — and said nothing. He marked it with a cairn of stacked stones only he would recognize, checks the cairn on every run, and has never once decided what to do if it changes.

entities.name: Silas Blackwood
entities.filed_from: From a Wake in Verrowen story
entities.body:
_From a Wake in Verrowen story, 2026-11-08 · Story._

**Character Profile:**

Name: Silas Blackwood (not found out yet)
Sex: Male
Race: Human
Age: Approximately 38 years old
Appearance: Tall and leanly built, with dark hair streaked with grey at the temples and piercing grey eyes that hold a deep sadness. He bears several scars - most notably a jagged wound across his left shoulder and a faint burn mark on his right hand – and wears worn leather clothing suited for travel and survival. 
Magic: Detection – a weak but responsive ability allowing him to sense residual magic and identify magical objects; he’s capable of limited shielding against mental intrusion.
Personality: Stoic, reserved, haunted by a profound sense of loss and burdened by fragmented memories. Prone to moments of intense focus and bursts of decisive action when under pressure. Deeply wary of others, but fiercely protective of those who earn his trust—a quality slowly emerging amidst his guarded exterior. 

Skills: Combat (proficient with knives), Tracking, Survival, Limited Magical Detection.
Background so far: Silas awoke with amnesia in a burned cottage high on the hillside outside Stoutwell, discovering a strange connection to an ancient silver locket and encountering unsettling remnants of forgotten magic. His initial disorientation is being replaced by a growing awareness of danger and a desperate need to uncover his past.
Key items: Silver Locket (containing portraits of a young boy and a weeping woman); Goblin Knife; Hearthstone.
Who they met: Murrow (artificer), Hesketh Reeve (Guard Captain), Wendeline Brackenford (Elder).
Places they've been: Ruined Cottage near Stoutwell.
Allies and enemies: None yet - potential allies are emerging through his encounters.
Debts and promises: Unknown – he hasn’t made any commitments beyond surviving.
Wounds and scars: Shoulder wound from an arrow, burn mark on right hand.
Open mysteries: The origin and purpose of the silver locket, the fragmented memories haunting him, the nature of the energy emanating from the hearthstone, the fate of the child depicted within the portrait.

The story so far: Silas Blackwood stumbled into a nightmare woven with snow, blood, and echoes of forgotten pain. He awoke disoriented, wounded, and stripped of all memory, only to discover a chilling connection to a vanished girl and a dangerous artifact—the silver locket. Driven by instinct and fueled by burgeoning magical abilities, he battled goblins guarding a ruined cottage, unearthed cryptic clues in a hidden journal, and confronted a torrent of unsettling visions triggered by the locket’s presence. As he attempted to understand these events, the faint hum resonating from the hearthstone grew stronger, hinting at a deeper mystery linked to Murrow, the artificer, and the shifting realities of the Grand Orrery. His journey has just begun, a descent into a world of ancient secrets and perilous possibilities. 

Silas is now a haunted man grappling with lost memories and nascent magic, driven to unravel the truth behind his amnesia and confront whatever forces seek to control him.

fields.label: A creature adapted to the damp, echoing depths of the Monster Wood, it communicates through subtle shifts in air pressure and uses this ability for both hunting and defense.
fields.what_it_is: A "Silken Stalker," a small, serpentine predator about the size of a large dog – roughly three feet long - covered in moss-like fur that blends perfectly with the Monster Wood’s undergrowth. It possesses delicate, membranous wings allowing short bursts of gliding flight.
fields.who: Native to the deepest sections of the Monster Wood, primarily dwelling amongst ancient, decaying trees near areas saturated with moisture and shadow. They are solitary creatures, rarely interacting with each other or venturing far from their chosen territories.
fields.where: Specifically found within pockets of the Monster Wood characterized by unusually high humidity—particularly around fallen logs, stagnant pools, and deep ravines where the sunlight struggles to penetrate. Their dens are typically constructed within hollowed-out tree roots or beneath dense tangles of vines.
fields.how_it_works: The Silken Stalker doesn't rely on sight or sound; instead, it detects its prey (small animals, birds, even unwary travelers) using specialized organs located along its flanks that sense minute changes in air pressure caused by movement. These ‘pressure whispers’ allow it to pinpoint targets with incredible accuracy, effectively creating a 3D “map” of its surroundings.  It can also use this ability defensively, releasing a concentrated burst of compressed air as a disorienting shockwave.
fields.limits: Its sensitivity is heavily affected by strong winds or turbulent airflow – making open spaces perilous. Magical interference, especially spells that create sonic vibrations, severely disrupts its sensory system, causing intense pain and disorientation. Prolonged exposure to fire causes its fur to burn rapidly, stripping away its camouflage and leaving it vulnerable. It cannot reliably track magic users - they simply appear as static noise.
fields.ties: Murrow has been observing the Silken Stalkers during his research

- Every month, after their shift ends and before retiring for the night, each member of the Guard must spend precisely five minutes meticulously polishing their shield with river clay – a ritual overseen by Captain Hesketh himself. It’s believed this process strengthens not just the metal, but also the bond between the soldier and his protection, warding against ill fortune and ensuring vigilance during the next patrol. This habit stems from an obscure Elderhold tradition dating back to the village's founding, when a particularly brutal goblin raid was repelled thanks to a newly polished shield reflecting moonlight directly into the attackers’ eyes. The practice now serves as both a practical maintenance task and a visible demonstration of discipline and loyalty within the Guard ranks, subtly reinforcing its authority.

entities.name: Murrow’s Secret

fields.what_it_is: A new villager – an extremely old artificer named Murrow – arrives in Stoutwell with a strange device called the Seeker’s Lodestone, seeking knowledge about the source of the village’s dried well and potentially uncovering a hidden connection between Stoutwell and the dangers beyond the Monster Wood.
fields.who: Murrow, an artificer over five hundred years old, is a secretive and guarded individual. He bears little resemblance to the stereotypical artificer from the lore books—he wears a dark hood to obscure his face, speaks rarely, and seems intensely focused on locating something specific within Stoutwell. Doric, the master blacksmith, is wary of him due to his unsettling calm demeanor and expertise with materials that seem impossibly ancient. Hesketh Reeve sees him as a potential threat, given his apparent knowledge of arcane matters and reluctance to share information.
fields.where: Murrow establishes a small workshop - Monstradius - near Murrow’s shop in the NW housing district, utilizing salvaged parts and ash wood (sourced from the Ashen Reach). He spends most of his time meticulously studying the Silent Well, examining its crumbling stone walls and attempting to use the Seeker's Lodestone to detect residual mana signatures. The lodestone itself appears to resonate faintly when brought near areas affected by the Blight or unusually strong elemental currents.
fields.how_it_works: The Seeker's Lodestone functions through detecting faint traces of lingering magical energy – specifically, it responds strongest to events tied to significant shifts in the world’s structure like those caused by rifts. It doesn’t actively *find* things; rather, it guides Murrow towards locations where such energies are concentrated. Using it requires careful concentration and a steady hand, draining the user’s mana rapidly—a single prolonged scan could leave someone weak and dizzy.  Murrow seems to be using Doric's iron featherhooks to help channel this process, creating specific patterns on the stone that amplify the lodestone’s detection abilities, but he refuses to explain how.
fields.limits: The Seeker’s Lodestone is highly sensitive and easily disrupted by other sources

entities.name: The Silent Offering
entities.filed_from: Made up by the AI in auto mode

fields.what_it_is: A daily ritual performed by the Wellhouse elves where they leave a single, perfectly formed river stone upon the dried well, accompanied by a whispered request for continued prosperity – a silent offering meant to appease whatever spirit might dwell within the now-empty water source.
fields.who: Primarily practiced by the four Wellhouse elves - Wendeline Brackenford, Fenwick Larkspur, Bertram Quillby, Ysolde Ambergate – though all villagers quietly observe with respect. Burn, the Wellhouse’s regular, sometimes joins them, usually after a particularly potent ale.
fields.where: Directly on the dry basin of the old Stoutwell well, located in the center of the village square, always near the Gathering Hall. It stands adjacent to the crumbling walls that once held back the water, a stark reminder of its loss.
fields.how_it_works: Each elf carefully selects a smooth, grey river stone from the nearby riverbank – stones are collected over several days. They then meticulously clean the well basin before placing the stone gently atop it, followed by a short, almost inaudible prayer or blessing (the exact wording varies between generations). The act takes approximately five minutes, during which time they remain motionless, facing the setting sun.
fields.limits: The effectiveness of this “offering” is entirely based on belief and tradition; there's no demonstrable magical effect. However, the ritual serves as a focal point for community goodwill and represents a tangible connection to the past and their ancestors.  The offering only has power if the person offering it *believes* it will work. If someone doubts it, nothing happens.
fields.ties: This custom directly links to the founding story of Stoutwell - the legend says the well dried up because the villagers forgot to offer respect to the spirit of the water. The elves’ arrival centuries ago was seen as a sign that their dedication would restore prosperity. Burn’s frequent presence at the well further solidifies the custom within the village’s culture.

fields.what_it_is: A stone owl statue with subtly shifting eyes that trigger a brief detection spell when something significant leaves the Monster Wood - only effective for “big” events like creatures or people, not smaller things like animals or lost items.
fields.who: Constructed by Murrow using ash wood from the Ashen Reach, imbued with his own limited detection magic. It’s currently maintained by Whisperwind, a halfling Watcher tasked with its upkeep.
fields.where: Situated atop the highest point on the western wall of Stoutwell, overlooking the entrance to the Monster Wood – specifically positioned to catch any sign of movement through the trees. The owl faces west.
fields.how_it_works: When a creature or person of considerable size (defined as roughly ten feet tall or larger) passes within a fifty-foot radius of the statue, the owl’s eyes briefly glow with pale blue light, triggering a short-range detection spell focused solely on the immediate area. This reveals the presence of magical signatures, but provides no details about what caused them—only a sense of "something else" is detected.  The effect lasts for one round and requires a successful Detection check (difficulty set by Murrow). Whisperwind refreshes the enchantment every few weeks with her own minor detection spells; this uses mana, so she must carefully monitor her reserves.
fields.limits: The statue's range is limited; it won't trigger if something simply walks past quickly. Its sensitivity is also low, meaning it can be easily overwhelmed by ambient magic in the woods. Critically, it *cannot* detect small creatures like goblins, rodents, or even large birds - only substantial things. It’s reliant on Whisperwind's continued maintenance, and the enchantment fades if not refreshed regularly. The statue itself does not speak or offer guidance beyond its triggered detection; its value lies purely in warning of potential threats.
fields.ties: This mechanism directly connects to Murrow's secretive research into locating other artificers and his concern about the Kingdom’s expansion – he fears that increased activity within the Monster Wood will draw unwanted attention from those who seek to exploit its resources. Hesketh Ree

fields.what_it_is: A spectral hound, native only to the immediate area around the Monster Wood and especially active near Rook’s Watch, that acts as a living early warning system for intruders or significant magical disturbances within a roughly half-mile radius. It doesn't attack, instead emitting mournful howls when something triggers its heightened state – often before any physical threat materializes.
fields.who: Primarily controlled by Whisperwind, the village’s appointed “Watcher” - essentially a conduit and amplifier for the Hound’s abilities, though not its creator. The Hound itself seems ancient and unbound by normal rules of life and death.
fields.where: Specifically located along the western edge of Stoutwell where the Monster Wood begins, particularly concentrated around Rook’s Watch, a small elevated platform built atop a naturally occurring rock formation overlooking the woods. Its range extends approximately ½ mile outwards from Rook’s Watch. The wood grows dense enough here that most inhabitants don’t venture this far without Guard escort.
fields.how_it_works: The Hound appears to be drawn to strong magical signatures—even faint ones—and areas with unusual energy fluctuations. When triggered, it emits three distinct types of howling: a low rumble signifying general unease; a high-pitched whine indicating immediate danger; and a sustained, sorrowful wail if the disturbance is unnatural (like magic gone wrong). Whisperwind can subtly adjust the Hound’s sensitivity, but only through focused meditation and quiet intention.  It requires constant attention, as extended periods of silence or distraction weaken its connection. A significant drain on mana is required for Whisperwind to sustain the contact – roughly equivalent to one hour of focused spellcasting.
fields.limits: The Hound's effectiveness is directly tied to Whisperwind’s ability to maintain focus. Loud noises, distractions, or emotional distress severely disrupt the link. It cannot “see” in the conventional sense, relying solely on sensory input filtered by its spectral awareness. Additionally, the Hound *cannot* predict the outcome of events – merely alert to their presence. Finally, prolonged exposure to the hound causes a dulling effect - those who stand near it for too long find themselves unusually sluggish and unable

entities.name: Monstradius’s Secret
entities.filed_from: Made up by the AI in auto mode

fields.what_it_is: The GuildScribe’s hall keeps a collection of unusual artifacts recovered from failed Rift expeditions – mostly worthless trinkets or monster parts - but amongst these items is a single, perfectly preserved chromatic drake egg, kept under lock and key within Murrow’s most secure chamber.
fields.who: Primarily Murrow himself, along with Silas Blackwood, the current Head Scribe, and a rotating team of junior scribes tasked with cataloging and guarding the collection.
fields.where: Deep within Murrow’s research building—a space accessed only via a magically reinforced door hidden behind a bookshelf in his shop—the egg rests inside a lead-lined case, constantly chilled by a low-level elemental ward to prevent premature hatching.
fields.how_it_works: Murrow believes the egg holds a fragment of Xan’s wildshape magic, potentially a source for understanding and controlling similar abilities, though he acknowledges its immense instability. He uses detection magic daily on the egg and the case to maintain containment, layering protections against accidental activation – any attempt to breach the ward causes localized tremors and minor elemental surges. The chill temperature slows the growth process, allowing him to study the creature without immediate danger.
fields.limits: The egg's volatile nature means prolonged exposure to warmth or strong magical energy could trigger an explosive release; opening the case requires precise timing and a specific sequence of runes known only to Murrow, as even a slight misstep could unleash a torrent of chromatic drake essence.
fields.ties: This project stems from Murrow's secretive obsession with preventing another Rift disaster like the "Floating Men" incident where a structure was pulled through. Silas Blackwood discovered fragments of this expedition during a recent inventory, prompting a renewed focus on containing anomalous materials before they become dangerous again. It connects directly to Murrow’s reluctance to reveal details about his origins or past expeditions, hinting at a far more extensive history than anyone suspects.

It isn’t precise; it indicates *presence* rather than pinpointing exact sources or types of magic. Prolonged use drains Murrow’s personal mana reserves very slowly, requiring him to replenish them through meditation or consumption of specific herbs.

fields.what_it_is: Murrow maintains a subtle, almost undetectable observation post within his shop, utilizing carefully calibrated Resonance Stone Devices to monitor fluctuations in mana signatures – specifically those originating from disturbances or monstrous activity within a half-mile radius. These devices don’t actively *detect* monsters, but rather register unnatural shifts in magical energy that correlate with their presence.
fields.who: Primarily Murrow himself, occasionally assisted by Burn during particularly long watches.
fields.where: A hidden chamber beneath the main floor of Monstradius’s workshop, accessible only through a disguised section of shelving stocked with seemingly random ingredients and components. fields.how_it_works: The Resonance Stone Device consists of interlocking rings of polished mirrorstone, each attuned to a specific frequency of mana. When disturbed by nearby magic—especially elemental surges or the raw power of a monster—the rings vibrate subtly, creating a complex pattern detectable only by Murrow’s trained senses and amplified via a small, intricately crafted amplifier made of brass and copper. entities.body:
_Made up by the AI in auto mode, 2026-11-08 · about a person who lives in Stoutwell._

- Silas Blackwood, a halfling clockmaker aged 68, lives amongst the slums south of Stoutwell’s center, where he crafts intricate timepieces – not for profit, but to meticulously track shifts in the wind and the position of the stars. He wants to understand why the village well dried up centuries ago, believing the answer lies hidden within the movements of celestial bodies. His greatest fear is that his obsessive work will ultimately reveal nothing, leaving him trapped in a cycle of fruitless observation. He maintains a wary friendship with Burn, the Wellhouse tavern regular, exchanging stories (and occasionally, spare gears) over tankards of stout ale.

fields.what_it_is: A small, intricately carved pipe crafted from ashwood harvested – suspiciously quickly – from the Ashen Reach. It appears to subtly shift colors depending on the ambient light, displaying faint hues of grey, brown, and even a fleeting violet.
fields.who: It was created by Silas Blackwood, a former apprentice artificer who vanished twenty years ago after being dismissed for “unorthodox experimentation.” He lived near Stoutwell, scavenging materials and obsessively studying the workings of Mundane objects.  Silas never sought riches or fame, only knowledge - particularly about how things held magic. Currently, he is known to be working within Monstradius's research building.
fields.where: Initially found in Silas’ workshop, located just outside the slums in Stoutwell. Now resides primarily within Murrow’s shop, though its exact location within the cluttered space remains… ambiguous.
fields.how_it_works: The pipe doesn't produce smoke when lit with normal fuel (even charcoal). Instead, it draws upon the ambient mana present in an object nearby, condensing it into a visible haze that shimmers with rainbow colours. This haze isn’t truly "smoke," but rather refined mana, cool to the touch and faintly smelling of rain-soaked stone. When used carefully, this condensed mana can temporarily enhance simple tasks: speeding up woodcutting, improving the precision of hammering, or briefly strengthening a fragile structure – effects mirroring Doric’s Featherhooks, but far weaker. Each use drains a small amount of Mana Affinity from the user; if they don’t have any latent affinity, the drain manifests as increased dizziness and coldness. If the user has affinity, there will be a subtle warming sensation followed by exhaustion.

In areas rich in natural mana (like near strong elemental sources), it can operate for several minutes at a time. However, in places devoid of magic - like inside the walls of Monstradius's building - it quickly becomes inert. Furthermore, prolonged use causes increasing fatigue and disorientation in Murrow. fields.what_it_is: Within the deepest reaches of the Monster Wood, near where the gnarled trees weep sap that glows with an unsettling green light, dwells a creature known only as Rook – a “Rootwraith,” a being formed entirely of intertwined tree roots animated by residual magic left behind by the blight. It doesn't actively hunt or attack, instead meticulously collecting dropped items - lost tools, broken weapons, scraps of clothing – arranging them in intricate patterns around specific, ancient oaks.
fields.who: Rook is not sentient in any traditional sense. It is a construct, a lingering echo of the blighted wood’s desperate attempt to defend itself, now driven purely by instinctual compulsion. It seems to be roughly humanoid in shape, standing about seven feet tall, its body composed of dark, twisted branches interwoven with glowing moss and thorny vines. The glow isn’t warm, more like sickly moonlight.
fields.where: Rook resides exclusively within a small clearing approximately five miles into the Monster Wood, marked by three particularly grotesque, weeping oak trees clustered together—these are the focal points for its collection efforts.  The area is perpetually shrouded in mist and choked with fungal growth; a rare pocket untouched by the Blight’s outer reach. Specifically, this clearing sits at the foot of the Brackwood Fringe, where the woods begin to feel truly alien.
fields.how_it_works: The Rootwraith’s movement is slow but relentless, powered by a subtle manipulation of the surrounding root systems. It can move silently through dense undergrowth, almost as if becoming part of the forest itself. Its primary “attack” mechanism involves ensnaring victims using rapidly extending roots – these aren't aggressive; they simply bind and restrain until the person becomes too exhausted to free themselves. Importantly, it doesn't seem to actively *consume* anything beyond what it collects, instead meticulously arranging them - items collected appear to create a complex map that shifts frequently.  It has no apparent weaknesses other than intense heat or fire--which seems to slowly burn away its form, though quickly re-forms.
fields.limits: The Rootwraith's influence weakens significantly outside of the immediate

entities.name: Silas’s Stone
entities.filed_from: Made up by the AI in auto mode

fields.what_it_is: A smooth, grey river stone etched with faint swirling patterns that faintly glow when held by someone experiencing intense emotion – primarily fear or grief. It seems to draw out these feelings before dampening them.
fields.who: Silas Blackwood, an elderly halfling peddler known for his oddly calming presence and unsettlingly accurate predictions about people’s moods. He acquired the stone from a wandering cleric during a particularly violent storm fifty years ago.
fields.where: Silas keeps the stone displayed prominently inside his wagon near the entrance to Stoutwell’s market square. He claims it helps him “understand” customers better, though some whisper he uses it to manipulate their desires.
fields.how_it_works: When someone holds the stone, they experience a brief surge of heightened emotional awareness—a sudden flood of sadness, anxiety, or even overwhelming joy. This intensity quickly subsides as the stone subtly absorbs the excess energy, leaving the user feeling strangely calm and detached. The stone doesn’t *cause* the emotions, merely amplifies them momentarily, then neutralizes the effect. Because magic in Verrowen is weak, this amplification relies on an existing wellspring of emotion within the holder.  It requires approximately 1 mana per minute of sustained use; prolonged exposure leads to exhaustion and dizziness.
fields.limits: The stone only affects those with a significant level of emotional vulnerability. Those shielded by strong willpower or practiced control will find it inert. It can also be overwhelmed by exceptionally intense emotions (like witnessing a horrific event), causing a feedback loop that drains the user's mana rapidly. Furthermore, once a person has experienced its full effect, they are temporarily immune - needing another twenty-four hours for the stone's influence to reassert itself.
fields.ties: Silas acquired the Stone from Father Benedict, who was tasked with comforting villagers during the Great Flood fifty years prior – Benedict vanished after the storm, his fate unknown but rumored to have been taken by one of the many monsters emerging from the Monster Wood. The swirling patterns etched into the stone bear a faint resemblance to maps depicting the routes used by lost travelers in the woods—a detail Silas never explains.

This isn’t simply patrolling; it involves a carefully orchestrated series of actions designed to detect unusual movement or disturbances within the wood.
fields.who: Currently, Rook is Silas Blackwood, an aging Guard veteran known for his unnervingly still demeanor and keen observation skills. He was chosen specifically for this role due to his quiet nature and experience dealing with unsettling creatures from the wood. His predecessor, Rook (a different man), vanished five years prior while on this post, leaving behind only whispers and unanswered questions.
fields.where: The vigil takes place in a small, concealed clearing just beyond the outermost wall of Stoutwell’s defenses, overlooking a particularly dense section of the Monster Wood where strange lights have been reported. It's marked by three standing stones arranged in a triangle— remnants of some forgotten purpose.
fields.how_it_works: Silas begins with a simple task: he sets up a network of Whisperwind watches, tiny mechanical birds that are set to fly out into the forest, spreading detection magic. Then, he uses his “Rook’s Vigil,” a ritual involving a complex pattern of hand gestures combined with slow, deliberate breaths which triggers a subtle amplification of his senses – allowing him to hear fainter sounds and perceive shifts in the air. Finally, at each hour after midnight, Silas will lay down a circle of bright white chalk around the clearing; if any creature steps inside or outside the chalk line, he immediately alerts the rest of the guard.
